# Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits; flag failing audits for producer review

**Headline:** The audit runner must stop re-arming `needsProducerReview` on a
passing re-audit of an item the producer has already reviewed, and must start
setting it on any failing (`Ready to close: No`) top-level audit — so a
producer's review survives a release-time re-audit while genuine failures
always reach the producer queue.

## Problem statement

On 2026-10-27 a `dev`→`main` release of the ContextHub store was blocked
because the audit runner re-flagged 14 top-level `in_review` items for producer
review. The producer had already reviewed and cleared those items; the release's
own re-audits all **passed**, and each pass unconditionally wrote
`--needs-producer-review yes`, silently discarding the producer's review.
Inversely, the failing-verdict path only flags an item when
`merge_gate_blocker` is set, so genuinely failing items never reach the
producer-review queue. The review state is unobservable after the fact because
`needsProducerReview` is a bare boolean and flag-only flips neither bump
`updatedAt` nor leave any record.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — the person who reviews and clears items before
  release. *"As a producer I want a review I have given to stay given until the
  item's content actually changes, so that I am not asked to re-approve the same
  unchanged work every time a release re-audits it."*
- **Producer, failure path** — *"As a producer I want every item whose audit says
  `Ready to close: No` surfaced to me, so that a failing item cannot sit
  silently in the actionable queue."*
- **Release gate (ship skill)** — *"As the release gate I want
  `needsProducerReview` to mean exactly 'this item needs producer attention now',
  so that the gate neither blocks on already-reviewed work nor passes
  unreviewed/unready work."*
- **Audit runner (agent)** — *"As the audit runner I want an unambiguous rule for
  when to set the flag, so that pass/fail lifecycles stay deterministic and
  auditable."*

## Target behaviour

| Verdict | Item | Prior producer review (signal present) | `needsProducerReview` after the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | yes (reviewed, content unchanged since review) | **left `false`** (do not re-flag) |
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | no (never reviewed, or content changed since review) | **`yes`** (current behaviour) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level (independent audit) | either | **`yes`** (generalise the merge-gate branch) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level, cascade-demotion-suppressed (parent-triggered re-audit of an `in_review`/`done` item) | either | **unchanged / never set** (producer decision, Q2 = no) |
| any | child (has parent) | either | **unchanged / never set** (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H) |

> **Cascade rule (producer decision Q2 = no).** A `No` produced by a
> parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item is not
> an independent review: the demotion is suppressed (SA-0MUJAPC680078396) and the
> flag is likewise left untouched. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the
> item to the producer.

Existing lifecycle guarantees are unchanged: pre-audit status/stage restore on
abort and on infrastructure failure, `updatedAt = auditedAt` on audit persist,
assignee clear-on-terminal, and the descendant cascade authorised only by a
verified `Yes`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (reviewed pass is preserved).** A passing verdict (`Ready to close: Yes`)
  on a top-level item whose producer has already reviewed it (and whose content
  is unchanged since that review) does not write
  `--needs-producer-review yes`; the stored `false` is preserved and the item is
  not re-entered into the producer-review queue.
- **AC2 (first pass still enters the queue).** A passing verdict on a top-level
  item that has never been reviewed still sets `needsProducerReview = yes`.
- **AC3 (independent failures always surface).** A failing verdict
  (`Ready to close: No`) from an **independent** audit of a top-level item sets
  `needsProducerReview = yes` regardless of whether `merge_gate_blocker` is set,
  and never clears an existing review. The single exception is the
  cascade-demotion-suppressed branch (Q2 = no): a parent-triggered re-audit of an
  already-`in_review`/`done` item leaves the flag untouched.
- **AC4 (signal is durable, auditable and content-scoped).** The review state used
  by AC1/AC3 distinguishes *"reviewed and cleared"* from *"never flagged"*, is
  recorded somewhere a later run (and a human) can inspect, and is invalidated
  when the item's reviewed content changes — so a materially changed item
  requires a fresh producer review.
- **AC5 (transitions covered by tests in the default suite).** Regression tests
  cover all four transitions — never-reviewed pass → flagged; reviewed pass →
  preserved; fail → flagged (with and without `merge_gate_blocker`); review →
  content change → pass → flagged again — and run in the default suite
  (`skill/audit/tests/`, no marker gating).
- **AC6 (children unchanged).** A passing verdict on a child item never sets
  `needsProducerReview`, and no child-item lifecycle behaviour changes.
- **AC7 (no lifecycle regressions).** The existing guarantees hold: pre-audit
  status/stage restore on abort and infrastructure failure, `updatedAt =
  auditedAt` on audit persist, assignee clear-on-terminal, cascade-demotion
  suppression, and the lifecycle readback verification.
- **AC8 (docs).** The audit skill's reference documentation
  (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` lifecycle section)
  states the pass/fail flag semantics explicitly, including that producer review
  is **content-scoped** and how a cleared flag is distinguished from a
  never-flagged item.
- **AC9 (documentation currency).** All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC10 (suite).** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Review-state signal — DECIDED: Option B+ (producer, 2026-10-28)

`needsProducerReview` alone cannot answer *"was this reviewed?"*. Two candidate
designs were carried into intake; the seed context marked Option A as preferred,
but the repository evidence gathered during intake changed the cost/benefit
picture (see *Existing state*), so the choice was put to the producer
(Appendix Q1). **Producer chose Option B+** — inference with the persisted-report
recap. Option A-lite remains a possible later upgrade but is **not** part of this
item's scope; it does not need to be raised as a dependency.

### Option B+ — infer from existing state, recap in the persisted report (no cross-repo change) — CHOSEN

At audit start, capture the item's pre-audit audit record (`readyToClose` +
`fingerprint`, both already exposed by `wl audit-show --json`) alongside the
existing pre-audit `wl show` capture. Then:

- prior audit `readyToClose == 1` **and** its fingerprint equals the current
  content fingerprint **and** the item's `needsProducerReview == false`
  → the flag can only have been cleared by a producer *after* that passing
  audit of identical content → **preserve `false`**;
- otherwise (no prior audit, prior audit failed, or content changed since the
  passing audit) → **flag `yes`**;
- `needsProducerReview == true` is never cleared by the runner.

Because the audit content fingerprint is already content-scoped (schema-2
sha256 over the item's own `title` + `description`), this option satisfies AC4's
*content-scoped* requirement with no schema change. For auditability, the runner
appends an explicit metadata line to the report it persists anyway
(e.g. `Producer review: preserved (content fingerprint <fp>)` /
`Producer review: required (reason)`), so the decision is recorded in the
durable audit record.

### Option A-lite — durable review marker in the worklog store (cross-repo; NOT chosen)

Add a nullable marker (e.g. `audit_results.producer_reviewed_fingerprint` +
`producer_reviewed_at`, or `work_items.producerReviewedAt`) written whenever
`needsProducerReview` transitions `true → false`. The audit runner then compares
the stored reviewed fingerprint with the current one: equal → preserve `false`;
different/absent → flag `yes`.

This is exact and self-documenting, but it is a ContextHub worklog change:
schema migration + repair-on-open + the marker must be written on **every**
clear path (`wl reviewed <id> false`, `wl update --needs-producer-review false`
used by the ship gate's remediation text, the ship override that clears child
flags, and any future path). It also creates a cross-repo blocking dependency
for this item.

**Cost signal:** Option B+ is a single-repo change (one lifecycle region, one
helper, tests, docs); Option A-lite additionally requires a ContextHub work
item, migration, CLI surface and its own audit. Option B+ can be upgraded to
Option A-lite later without changing this item's acceptance criteria for the
pass/fail rules. **Not chosen by the producer — no ContextHub dependency is
raised by this item.**

## Constraints

- **Do not revert the pass-flag contract.** SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5 and
  SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW established that an automated pass puts a top-level item in
  the producer queue; this item refines *when*, not *whether*.
- **Never clear a review silently.** The runner may preserve `false`; it must not
  write `--needs-producer-review no` on any path.
- **Fail-safe direction.** When the review signal is ambiguous or unavailable
  (e.g. `wl audit-show` fails, legacy fingerprint-less audit), the runner must
  fall back to **flagging** (`yes`) — a spurious review request is a nuisance; a
  silently discarded review gate is a release-safety defect.
- **Bias to fewer `wl` calls.** No new per-item `wl` invocation on the hot path
  where the existing freshness gate already fetched the audit record; the
  forced path (`--force` / `--refresh-audits`) adds exactly one `wl audit-show`.
- **Children remain exempt** from the flag (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H).
- No new user-facing CLI flags; no change to how a producer clears the flag.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the passing-verdict lifecycle
  (~13576–13600) appends `["--needs-producer-review", "yes"]` for every
  top-level item with no reference to prior review state; the failing-verdict
  lifecycle (~13626–13660) adds the same flag **only** under
  `if ctx.merge_gate_blocker:` in the demotion branch.
- The runner already fetches everything needed for the decision: `wl show` at
  ~10247 yields `ctx.wi` (including `parentId` and `needsProducerReview`), and
  the pre-audit `original_status` / `original_stage` capture (~10238–10256) is
  the natural home for a pre-audit audit-record capture.
- `_check_audit_freshness` (~2085–2160) already runs `wl audit-show <id> --json`
  on the non-forced path and compares the stored v2 content fingerprint with the
  recomputed one — the same data Option B+ needs. The forced path
  (`--force`, `--refresh-audits`, batch drains) bypasses the gate, so an explicit
  capture is required there.
- `audit_results` (ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts` ~305–315) already stores
  `ready_to_close`, `audited_at`, `fingerprint`; `wl audit-show --json` exposes
  `fingerprint` (`src/commands/audit-result.ts`). `wl list --json` additionally
  emits a recomputed `currentFingerprint` via `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`
  (parity-tested against the Python algorithm).
- The audit content fingerprint is **item-data-only** (schema 2: sha256 over
  `title` + `description`) — comments and flag flips do not contribute, so a
  review-clear or a comment cannot invalidate a stored fingerprint.
- ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed.ts` is a flag-only flip; the ship gate's
  remediation guidance (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` ~506–530) and
  `run-release.js` (~668–710) clear flags with `wl update <id>
  --needs-producer-review false`. A durable marker (Option A-lite) would have to
  hook **all** of these, not just `wl reviewed`.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` lives in **ContextHub**, not SorraAgents (the seed's Key
  Files section lists it without a repo; `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
  `skill/audit/SKILL.md` are the SorraAgents-side surfaces).
- The flag-only-flip contract ("flips of `needsProducerReview` do not bump
  `updatedAt`", `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` ~260) means `updatedAt` **cannot** be used
  as a review timestamp — it is bumped by the audit persist itself.
- Current behaviour is pinned by tests that must be updated with the fix:
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (pass-with-hold cases at
  ~239, ~306, ~521, ~544), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` ~436
  (cascade pass still flags), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`
  (fail-flag cases ~523–700).
- The mock harness `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py`
  (`stateful_wl_side_effect`) deliberately passes `audit-show` through untouched
  — it needs a pre-audit audit-record knob so the new rules can be exercised.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

1. **Capture pre-audit audit state** next to the existing pre-audit `wl show`
   capture: `prior_audit = {readyToClose, fingerprint, auditedAt}` (reuse the
   freshness gate's fetch on the non-forced path; one `wl audit-show` otherwise).
   Capture failure ⇒ treat as "no prior audit" (fail-safe → flag).
2. **Add one predicate** (e.g. `_producer_review_preserved(wi, prior_audit)`)
   implementing the chosen signal from the *Review-state signal* section, with a
   single documented truth table. Pure function, unit-testable without the model.
3. **Passing branch**: keep `--needs-producer-review yes` for top-level items
   **unless** the predicate holds, in which case append nothing (preserve the
   stored `false`). Log the decision (stderr + the persisted report line) with the
   reason and fingerprint. The rule is identical for items already at a terminal
   `done` stage (those keep their stage and only gain/lose the flag).
4. **Failing branch (independent `No`)**: emit `--needs-producer-review yes` for
   every top-level `No` verdict — merge-gate-blocked *and* ordinary `No` — keeping
   the existing merge-gate behaviour and adding the general case. Never emit `no`.
   This applies **only** when `_cascade_suppress_demotion` is false (see step 5).
5. **Unchanged branches**: infrastructure-failure restore and cascade-demotion
   suppression keep the flag untouched (no set, no clear) — record this explicitly
   in comments so a future edit does not "helpfully" flag on a timeout or a
   parent-triggered cascade. Per the producer's Q2 answer, a cascade-suppressed
   `No` does **not** flag even when `merge_gate_blocker` is set: the
   `--needs-producer-review yes` must move inside the non-suppressed demotion
   branch (a merge-gate failure that matters is re-surfaced by the next
   independent audit).
6. **Children**: no change (no flag on pass, existing behaviour elsewhere).
7. **Dry-run parity**: `--do-not-persist` still applies the flag rules; the
   persisted-report line is skipped (no report is stored).
8. **Tests** (default suite, `skill/audit/tests/`): extend the mock harness with a
   prior-audit knob, then add the four transition tests (AC5) plus child
   regression, merge-gate parity, the cascade-suppressed-`No`-does-not-flag case
   (Q2), and an "audit-show unavailable ⇒ flagged" fail-safe test.
9. **Docs**: update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (add a "Producer-review
   flag lifecycle / content-scoped review" section) and
   `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~35, ~85 lifecycle text), including the chosen option
   and the fail-safe rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — passing-verdict lifecycle (~13576–13600), failing-verdict lifecycle (~13626–13660), pre-audit capture (~10238–10256), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` (~2085–2230). Needs the pre-audit audit-record capture, the new predicate and both flag rules.
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — report persistence; needs the "Producer review: preserved/required" metadata line (Option B+).
- `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py` — mock harness; needs a prior-audit/`audit-show` knob.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`, `test_audit_runner_review.py`, `test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` — pinned expectations to update plus the new transition tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~35, ~85) — user-facing lifecycle description.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — implementation reference; new producer-review lifecycle section.
- **Not in scope (Option A-lite, rejected by the producer):** ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts`, `src/commands/reviewed.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`/`migrations/` — no worklog schema or CLI change is made by this item, and no cross-repo dependency is raised.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision 1 (cascade, producer Q2 = no).** A `No` verdict produced by a
  parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item does
  **not** set the flag — the flag follows the demotion: suppressed demotion ⇒ no
  flag. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the item to the producer. Note
  this deliberately narrows the merge-gate branch too: a cascade-suppressed
  merge-gate `No` does not flag (the next independent audit re-surfaces it).
- **Assumption 1 (infrastructure failure).** An infrastructure-failure restore
  leaves `needsProducerReview` untouched (neither set nor cleared): a model
  timeout must never manufacture a producer-review request nor discard a review
  (producer Q3 = yes).
- **Assumption 2 (fail-safe).** Any ambiguity in the review signal resolves to
  *flag* (`yes`), never to *preserve* (`false`).
- **Assumption 3 (scope).** Only the audit runner's lifecycle writes the flag;
  the ship gate's own clearing/escalation paths (`check-audit-gate.js`,
  `check-final-validation.js`, `run-release.js`) are out of scope and unchanged.
- **Risk: derived signal (Option B+).** Without a stored review marker, a
  human cannot see *when* the producer reviewed, only that the flag is `false`
  over an unchanged passing audit. Mitigation: the persisted report line records
  the decision + content fingerprint, and Option B+ upgrades cleanly to Option
  A-lite later.
- **Risk: stale fixture expectations.** The current suite pins the unconditional
  flag in ≥6 places; a rushed edit could "fix" the tests instead of the
  behaviour. Mitigation: each test states which of AC1–AC6 it pins.
- **Risk: extra `wl` latency.** Mitigation: reuse the freshness gate's fetch;
  at most one added `wl audit-show` per forced audit.
- **Accepted edge (Option B+).** A flag cleared by an automated override rather
  than a human (the ship gate's child remediation, or the post-release close
  step) is indistinguishable from a human review. Both are intentional clears and
  preserving them is the correct outcome, so no attempt is made to tell them
  apart.
- **Risk: cascade failures are surfaced later, not immediately (Q2 = no).** A
  failing cascade re-audit no longer flags, so a genuine problem found only by a
  cascade pass reaches the producer at the next independent audit. Mitigation:
  the cascade run already prints its suppression notice to stderr and the
  persisted report keeps the `No` verdict visible on the item.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Related improvements spotted during implementation
  (e.g. a producer-review audit trail across the whole worklog, a
  `wl review-history` command) are recorded as separate work items, not folded
  into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (no parent) *(completed)*: narrowed the flag to top-level
  items; its child exemption is preserved by AC6.
- **SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5** — Audit runner: set needsProducerReview on 'yes'
  verdicts *(completed)*: introduced the unconditional pass flag this item
  refines.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item ready to close *(completed)*: the original contract.
- **SA-0MS4TXDPR006HO2W** — Update documentation for producer-review gating
  *(completed)*: the docs this item extends.
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** — merge-gate fail-closed flag on integration failure:
  the `merge_gate_blocker` branch generalised by AC3.
- **SA-0MUJAPC680078396** — cascade-audit demotion suppression (relevance:
  Decision 1 — the flag follows the demotion).
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT / SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP** — audit content fingerprint and
  the item-data-only (v2) formula: the content-scoping mechanism AC4 reuses.

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** – Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for top-level items (no parent) (completed)
- **SA-0MS4TXDPR006HO2W** – Update documentation for producer-review gating (completed)
- **SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5** – Audit runner: set needsProducerReview on 'yes' verdicts (revert assignee-hold producer marking, keep assignee clear-on-terminal) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~220 further tokens)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~215 further tokens)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~192 further tokens)

## Evidence (reproduction)

1. Create a top-level item and audit it to a passing verdict → `needsProducerReview = yes` (AC2 behaviour).
2. `wl reviewed <id> false` (or `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) → flag clears, `updatedAt` unchanged.
3. Re-audit the unchanged item to a passing verdict (or run the ship gate's `--refresh-audits`) → observed: `needsProducerReview` flips back to `yes` with `updatedAt == auditedAt`. Expected after the fix: stays `false`.

Inspect the flag at any point with:

```bash
wl show <id> --json | jq '{needsProducerReview: .workItem.needsProducerReview, updatedAt: .workItem.updatedAt}'
wl audit-show <id> --json | jq '.audit | {readyToClose, auditedAt, fingerprint}'
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py check-freshness <id>   # read-only probe
```

Observed on 2026-10-27 for WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P, WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8,
WL-0MVK0UO3Q002TXW6, WL-0MVMZP6A5005PB66, WL-0MVMSE2S0006L56D, WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0,
WL-0MVMSE5LN003KCPQ, WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1, WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX, WL-0MVOTIJ2U000JI44,
WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG, WL-0MVPRZU0A000TSWD, WL-0MVM92MZ50075E6B.

<!-- discovered-from: ContextHub release attempt 2026-10-27 (dev→main blocked by spurious producer-review flags) -->

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (review-state signal, blocking):** *"`needsProducerReview` alone cannot
  answer 'was this reviewed?'. Choose the review-state signal: (a) **Option B+** —
  infer from the stored passing audit + unchanged content fingerprint, and recap
  the decision in the persisted report (no cross-repo change, ~1 day); (b)
  **Option A-lite** — add a durable `producer_reviewed_at` + fingerprint marker
  written on every `true → false` transition (exact, but a ContextHub schema +
  CLI change, raising a cross-repo dependency and blocking this item)."*
  **Recommended:** Option B+ — the v2 content fingerprint already stored on
  `audit_results` makes the inference content-scoped, so AC4 is met without a
  worklog schema change or a cross-repo blocker; Option A-lite remains a clean
  later upgrade.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28): "b+" — Option B+ chosen.** Option A-lite is
  rejected for this item: no ContextHub schema/CLI change and no cross-repo
  dependency. Research evidence: inspected `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  lifecycle + `_check_audit_freshness`, ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed.ts`,
  `src/persistent-store.ts` `audit_results`, `src/commands/audit-result.ts`,
  `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`; summarised in *Existing state*.
- **Q2 (cascade behaviour):** *"Should a `No` verdict from a parent-triggered
  cascade re-audit of a top-level item also set the flag, even though the
  demotion is suppressed?"*
  **Recommended:** Yes — demotion suppression protects workflow position, the
  flag protects release safety.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28): "no" — the producer overruled the
  recommendation.** A cascade-suppressed `No` leaves `needsProducerReview`
  untouched (no flag), including when `merge_gate_blocker` is set; the flag
  follows the demotion. Implemented as Decision 1 in *Risks & assumptions* and
  as the cascade row of the *Target behaviour* table.
- **Q3 (infrastructure-failure behaviour):** *"May a timeout/infrastructure-failure
  restore leave `needsProducerReview` untouched (never set, never cleared)?"*
  **Recommended:** Yes — a transient failure must not manufacture a review
  request nor discard one.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28): "yes" — confirmed**; recorded as Assumption 1
  in *Risks & assumptions* and step 5 of *Desired change*.

## Effort and Risk (estimated on Option B+ — the signal chosen by the producer)

- **T-shirt size:** Small
- **PERT:** O=4.50h, M=7.00h, P=13.00h → **expected 7.58h**, recommended
  **11.58h** with overheads (coordination 0.5, review 1.0, testing 1.0, risk
  buffer 1.5); range 8.50h–17.00h
- **WBS:** audit_runner lifecycle change 3.33h; regression tests + mock harness
  3.17h; documentation 1.08h
- **Risk:** score 13/25 — High (probability 3.16/5, impact 4.21/5); confidence
  74%
- **Cost of Option A-lite instead:** adds a ContextHub schema migration, CLI
  surface, cross-repo blocking dependency and its own audit — approximately
  double the effort, plus a release-ordering constraint (this item cannot land
  before the worklog change). Rejected by the producer, so not incurred.
- **Effect of the Q2 answer on this estimate:** negligible — moving
  `--needs-producer-review yes` inside the non-suppressed demotion branch and
  adding one cascade test is a sub-hour delta within the estimate's range; the
  figure above is unchanged.

## Problem

A full-project  run reports fixes that were never applied.

Observed on 2026-10-28 (SorraAgents @ dev):
- Report claimed `Auto-fixed: 8`, listing EXE005, ISC004, PLW1510 and RUF059 findings.
- `git status` afterwards showed **no source changes at all** (only the unrelated `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` scheduled-prompt timestamp).

Verified cause: those diagnostics are *not* auto-fixable (`ruff check --fix` reports `fix: null` for EXE005/PLW1510/RUF059 and `fix.applicability: unsafe` for ISC004).

## Root cause

`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `_parse_ruff_fix_output` (line ~113) converts **every** diagnostic in ruff's JSON output into a `fixed_findings` entry, without inspecting `item['fix']` or `item['fix']['applicability']`. `auto_fix_files` (line ~217) then sets `fixes_applied = len(fixed_findings) > 0` and the report prints those as auto-fixes. Ruff emits all diagnostics (fixed and unfixed) in its JSON output, so the count is the number of *diagnostics seen*, not fixes applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output` has the same shape (counts every message; eslint's `output`/`fixed` fields are ignored).

## Expected behaviour

- Only count a finding as auto-fixed when the linter actually applied an edit: ruff `item['fix']` is not `None` **and** `fix.applicability == 'safe'` (the default for `--fix` without `--unsafe-fixes`).
- Unfixable/unsafe diagnostics should either be dropped or surfaced as *remaining* smells, so they still reach smell detection, REFACTOR comments and work items.
- `fixes_applied`, the summary's `auto_fixed` count and the human-readable report must agree with what actually changed on disk.
- Add a regression test: a file with only-unsafe / no-fix diagnostics must report `Auto-fixed: 0`, and a file with a safe fix must report `Auto-fixed: 1` and be changed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output` only records findings whose fix is present and safe.
2. A full-project run against a tree whose only diagnostics are unsafe/unfixable reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A tree with one safe fix reports `Auto-fixed: 1` and the file is modified on disk.
4. Unsafe/unfixable diagnostics are still represented in the `Remaining smells` section (or equivalent) rather than silently dropped.
5. New unit tests in `skill/refactor/tests/` cover both cases.
6. Existing `skill/refactor` tests pass.

## Notes

Discovered from the `/skill:refactor` full-scan scheduled run. The 8 flagged diagnostics are already tracked by open REFACTOR items (SA-0MVRCL0Q90016C7D, SA-0MVRBPVU1001NGDW, SA-0MVRBPY7J004GJAI, SA-0MVPTU9HG00146UV), so this item is only about report/labelling accuracy.

data.description:
Counterpart of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81**
(`discovered-from:AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81`). The defect is in agent infrastructure in this
repository — `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The full discovery context (observed
drive run, timeout, unrelated commits landing on `dev`) is on the AI_Hell report; this
item is the actionable fix.

## Headline

`implement.py parent` decides whether a child worktree contains work via
`_git_path_has_changes()`, which reports "has changes" whenever the worktree `HEAD`
*differs* from the parent branch. A child worktree that is merely **behind** `dev`
(HEAD != `dev`, zero commits ahead, no dirty files) is therefore classified as having
work, and `phase_parent` immediately runs `finish` on empty work — which falls back to a
full-suite run when changed-scope selection is unavailable and can fail the whole parent
run.

## Problem statement

`_git_path_has_changes(path, parent_branch, expected_dirty=())` currently returns:

1. `True` when the worktree has dirty files (outside `.worklog/` and any
   project-declared expected-dirty prefixes), else
2. the result of comparing `git rev-parse HEAD` with `git rev-parse <parent_branch>`
   (differing ⇒ `True`), and
3. `True` (fail open) when either `rev-parse` fails.

Comparison (2) conflates *ahead* with *diverged*: a clean worktree at the fork base
after three unrelated commits landed on `dev` differs from `dev` but contains no work.

Observed 2026-10-19 during the AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV epic (details on
AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81):

1. `implement.py drive` started a child and the child session was killed at the 3600 s
   timeout with a clean worktree (no edits, no commits).
2. While the drive ran, three unrelated commits landed on `dev`; the child worktree was
   three commits behind.
3. `implement.py parent` reported `Child <id> has changes — running finish subprocess...`
   and ran `finish` on empty work; the changed-scope selection was unavailable, the full
   suite (~10 min under load) failed, and the run reported `Failed to finish child`.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree with no dirty files and **no commits ahead of** the parent branch is treated
as "no work" (the child is returned as `next_child` for implementation), regardless of
how far behind it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `_git_path_has_changes()` returns `False` for a worktree with no uncommitted
  changes and no commits ahead of the parent branch, including when the worktree is
  behind the parent branch (covered by unit tests against real throwaway git
  repositories/worktrees).
- **AC2:** `phase_parent` does not launch a `finish` subprocess for a child whose
  worktree is behind `dev` but has no local commits; the child is reported as the next
  child to implement (unit test).
- **AC3:** Worktrees with commits ahead, or with dirty files, are still detected as
  having changes (no regression; unit tests).
- **AC4:** The documented placement-guard contract
  (`docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` §"The placement guard") is preserved: a non-terminal
  child whose worktree is clean at the parent HEAD while the main checkout holds
  uncommitted changes outside `.worklog/` still fails closed, and a worktree that holds
  the work never triggers the guard (unit tests).

## Implementation plan

1. **Tests first** — add `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py`: clean at
   fork base, clean behind the parent branch, dirty file, one commit ahead, the
   `phase_parent` no-`finish` case, and the placement-guard cases (clean behind-only
   child + dirty main checkout fails closed; a worktree holding the work never triggers
   the guard). Confirm they fail against the current helper before changing it.
2. `_git_path_has_changes()` — keep the dirty-file check; replace the `HEAD != parent`
   comparison with an ahead-count test
   (`git rev-list --count <parent_branch>..HEAD` > 0). Keep failing open when the count
   cannot be computed (missing ref, git error).
3. Update the docstring (and `_has_worktree_changes()`'s docstring) to "dirty **or
   commits ahead of** the parent branch".
4. Verify the two guard call sites that consume the helper
   (`_worktree_placement_violation` in `phase_finish`, `_child_main_checkout_violation`
   in `phase_parent`/`phase_drive`) still match the documented contract (AC4); the
   step-1 tests pin the behaviour.
5. Update `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` if any wording still implies the "HEAD
   differs" rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_extension.py`
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`

## Risks and assumptions

- The ahead-count semantics also change the placement guards' view of a behind-only
  clean worktree: with unrelated main-checkout dirt present, such a child now fails
  closed as "work done outside the worktree" instead of being silently re-run. This
  matches the documented guard contract (AC4) but should be called out in the commit
  message; if it proves disruptive for long-running drives, file a follow-up.
- Assumes the worktree's `dev` ref is available locally (it is: worktrees share the main
  checkout's refs).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs
- Failing commit: d639d615
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
transcription failed: No module named 'numpy' — 9 unit subtests fail; the worker imports numpy at pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:117 and the host python3 (/usr/bin/python3, 3.12, no venv) cannot import it. pytest + node tests/node + node tests/cli all pass; only tests/unit fails.
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout d639d615`
2. Run the failing test through the test skill (changed scope, unit type) — or directly `node --test tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` from a non-agent shell
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

Reproduce without leaving the current checkout (numpy-free simulation): any interpreter whose `import numpy` fails, e.g. `python3 -S -c "import numpy"` (verified on the planning host: plain `python3` imports numpy 2.5.1 from the user site-packages, `python3 -S` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`).

## Root Cause Analysis (plan phase)

- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:115` `pcm_to_float32()` performs a lazy `import numpy as np` (`:117`); it is called from `TranscriptionSession` on every partial/final transcription (`:194`).
- The import is undeclared and unchecked: nothing validates numpy at `start`, so a numpy-free interpreter surfaces it only mid-stream as `{"type": "error", "message": "transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'"}` (`:334`, `:344`) — which fails 9 lifecycle subtests instead of producing an actionable startup error the way a missing `faster_whisper` does (`:268`–`:283`).
- The harness (`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs:58`–`:70`) is deliberately hermetic for `faster_whisper` (stub module injected through `PYTHONPATH`) but injects nothing for numpy, and spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` (`:31`) — i.e. whatever host interpreter is on `PATH`. Green on this host only because the developer's `python3` happens to carry numpy via the user site-packages.
- The documented contract is wrong: `docs/dev/voice-input.md:256`–`264` states the worker tests need no dependency install ("inject a stub `faster_whisper` module via `PYTHONPATH` … without the dependency installed"). numpy is a real, transitive hard requirement of faster-whisper, so it is present in any environment where the worker can do useful work — it is simply not declared, not checked, and not stubbed.
- Related prior art (not a duplicate — that item's scope is `wl sync` identity/purge): SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC comment 2026-10-15 records the same red suite on a host whose "system python3 lacks numpy", where "no passwordless sudo + PEP 668 externally-managed" made installing it impossible. The environment cannot be fixed from the repo, so harness hermeticity is the only durable fix.

## Key Files:

- pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py
- tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs
- docs/dev/voice-input.md

## Minimal Implementation:

1. Test-first (red): add a minimal `numpy` stub module to the temp stub directory created in the test's `before()` hook, exposing just what the worker uses (`frombuffer(data, dtype="<i2")` → an object with `.astype("float32")` and float division returning a sequence that supports `len()`), and add a subtest that runs the worker against a stub dir whose `numpy.py` raises `ImportError` and asserts an actionable `error` message at `start` (not a mid-stream `transcription failed`).
2. Worker: hoist the numpy availability check next to the existing `faster_whisper` import handling so a missing numpy produces the same actionable `error` at `start` (`:268`–`:283`), keeping the numpy-free import path for module import/doctor use.
3. Docs: correct `docs/dev/voice-input.md` — the test table plus the stub note must say both `faster_whisper` and `numpy` are stubbed, and numpy is listed as a runtime requirement of the worker.
4. Verification: run the changed-scope tests through the test skill; confirm the worker suite is green with a numpy-free interpreter and that no subtest is skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` passes on an interpreter that cannot import numpy: the harness supplies a stub numpy through the same `PYTHONPATH` stub directory used for `faster_whisper`, so all lifecycle subtests pass (no skips, no `.skip`) with no site-packages numpy available.
2. A missing numpy is reported as an actionable `error` message at `start` (same treatment as a missing `faster-whisper`), and a subtest covers it — the worker no longer emits `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` mid-stream.
3. `docs/dev/voice-input.md` documents the numpy runtime requirement and that the unit tests stub both `faster_whisper` and `numpy` (documentation matches the harness).
4. The full project test suite passes with the changes (dev-push gate green), and the fix is validated on the affected host as well as locally.

## Assumptions

- A1: Hermeticity is fixed in the test harness rather than by removing numpy from the worker. numpy is a hard transitive dependency of faster-whisper and `pcm_to_float32()` is the hot path for every partial/final transcription, so replacing it with a pure-Python conversion would add production risk for no user-visible benefit.
- A2: Extending the existing "missing dependency → actionable error, not a crash" behaviour from `faster-whisper` to numpy is treated as in-scope for this triage item (it is the message that made this failure look like a transcription bug); it is a few lines beside the existing handler. If the producer prefers the strictly minimal stub-only fix, AC2 can be dropped without affecting ACs 1, 3 and 4.
- A3: No environment remediation (installing numpy via sudo/pip) is part of this item — SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC documents that the affected host has no passwordless sudo and PEP 668 blocks it.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun the test through the test skill once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue. (Not flaky: deterministic on any numpy-free interpreter.)

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- Voice-input design: docs/dev/voice-input.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does the failure reproduce on the planning host? Answer (planning agent, 2026-10-28): not directly — plain `python3` imports numpy 2.5.1 from `~/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages`. Evidence: `python3 -c "import numpy"` succeeds, `python3 -S -c "import numpy"` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. The failure is environment-dependent and always reproducible when the spawned interpreter has no numpy, which is why AC1 requires the harness to supply it.
- Q: Is numpy required in production? Answer (planning agent, from `faster-whisper` dependency semantics and the worker code): yes — faster-whisper itself depends on numpy and `pcm_to_float32()` feeds `WhisperModel.transcribe()`. Evidence: `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:115`–`119`, `:194`.
- Q: Is this a duplicate of prior work? Answer: no. `wl search "whisper worker numpy"` returned only SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC, whose ACs cover `wl sync` GitHub identity authorisation and history purge; it mentions this suite only as a blocked-push deviation. Evidence: `wl show SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC --json`.
- No OPEN QUESTION entries: no producer input was required for this size of fix (effort Extra Small / risk Low).

Discovered during LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 (llm worklog) via test-failure SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ.

## Problem
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and exercises the real `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, which imports `numpy` (line 117). The repo declares no Python dependency manifest (no `requirements.txt`), so on a bare interpreter the whole unit node suite fails with `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` — the failure was red on this host from 2026-10-15 until numpy was installed ad hoc during the item above.

## Goal
As a maintainer, I want the voice-input worker's Python dependencies declared (and/or the unit test to skip with a clear message when they are absent), so a fresh checkout's full suite is green without undocumented host setup.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The worker's Python runtime dependencies (numpy, faster-whisper) are declared in a committed manifest (e.g. `pi-client/voice-input/requirements.txt`) and referenced from the voice-input README setup table.
2. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` either documents the install step in its header or skips (with an explicit, non-silent message) when the resolved interpreter cannot import the required modules.
3. Full suite is green on an interpreter provisioned only from the committed manifest (verified via the test skill; no ad-hoc pip installs).

## Out of scope
Changing the worker's transcription behaviour or its stub-based test contract.

## Related
- SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ — the test-failure item that surfaced this.
- LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 — llm worklog item whose dev-push gate was blocked by it (code in SorraAgents).

data.description:
# implement.py parent/drive starts children of a parent whose own outbound depends-on edge is unmet

discovered-from:RISE-0MVPY83CA00335W3 (TCE repo, cross-project reference only — the
edge below is recorded in the TCE worklog; the bug lives in this repo's
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

## Problem statement

`phase_parent()` / `phase_drive()` build their dependency graph **only from the
children's own outbound (`depends-on`) edges** (`wl_dep_blockers(cid)` per child
at `implement.py:5688`). The parent item's **own** outbound edges are never
consulted, and the parent's `status: blocked` is never checked. So a parent that
is deliberately `blocked` on an unmet dependency (a producer-mandated sequencing
hold) will still have its first startable child **started**, a worktree created,
and code implemented — silently overriding the producer's decision and editing
files the still-pending dependency is working on.

Real-world repro: TCE epic **RISE-0MVPY83CA00335W3** (*Remove the obsolete
'latestDeath' progression mechanic*) has `status: blocked` with outbound edge
→ **RISE-0MVN2V6YO002AHL4** (`in-progress`, itself an epic with 4 non-terminal
children editing the same files), per producer decision "land after
RISE-0MVN2V6YO002AHL4" (P-Q3=B, 2026-10-28). `/skill:implement
RISE-0MVPY83CA00335W3` was dispatched while the item was `blocked`; evaluation
showed `phase_parent` would classify F1 (`RISE-0MVRZKAKN002SFWM`, open) as
startable and create its worktree, ignoring the unmet edge. Verification code
path: `wl_dep_blockers` has a single call site (child classification); neither
`phase_start`, `phase_parent` nor `phase_drive` consults the parent's own
outbound edges or its status.

Note the distinction from SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T's documented assumption:
"cross-project external blockers are coordination notes" — that covers edges
recorded **on children** to other repos. This gap is a **same-project edge on
the parent itself**, which currently is not even reported, and a parent-level
`blocked` status that gates nothing.

## Users

- **Producer** — "As a producer, I want my explicit sequencing decisions
  (`depends-on` edges, `blocked` status, P-Q3-style holds) respected by the
  implement orchestrator, so a `blocked` epic never starts editing the same
  files an in-progress dependency still owns."
- **Agent/operator** — "As an agent, I want the orchestrator to tell me why a
  parent cannot start children (blocked by <id>), instead of creating a
  conflicting worktree mid-flight."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `phase_parent` (and therefore `phase_drive`) resolves the parent's own outbound edges via `wl_dep_blockers(<parent>)` **before** classifying any child. If any outbound blocker is non-terminal, no child worktree is created; the report carries a `parent_blocked_by` list (ids + statuses), and the per-child classifications are skipped/reported as blocked. `phase_start` on a leaf whose own outbound edges are unmet behaves likewise.
2. A parent with `status: blocked` and an unmet outbound edge produces a `blocked` verdict (not `ok` + `next_child`) dedicated to that reason; the automation-friendly JSON includes the blocker ids.
3. Behaviour is unchanged when the parent has no outbound edges or all outbound blockers are terminal (`_is_terminal_child` semantics) — no regression to the existing in-chain ordering (SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J) or parent-advance rules.
4. Regression tests cover: (a) parent blocked by one non-terminal outbound blocker → no child started, report names the blocker; (b) parent with terminal/absent outbound blockers → prior behaviour; (c) leaf item whose own blockers are unmet → start refuses with the blocker list.
5. `SKILL.md` Step 6.1 documents that a parent whose own outbound blockers are unmet waits (mirrors the portrait of `wl next` / `blocked` status), and the external-blocker "coordination note" wording is clarified to include same-project parent-level edges.

## Minimal implementation

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `phase_parent` (~line 5569): after fetching the parent (Step 3), call
    `parent_blockers = wl_dep_blockers(work_item_id)`; **before** Step 5
    (child classification), if any outbound blocker is non-terminal
    (`_is_terminal_status` / hard-deleted semantics from `_is_terminal_child`),
    emit the `blocked`-verdict report (`parent_blocked_by` = ids + statuses; no
    `next_child`, no worktree creation) and return early. Terminal or
    soft-deleted blockers are ignored.
  - `phase_drive` (~line 6637): when a parent report carries
    `parent_blocked_by`, copy it into the drive report and stop **without**
    spawning a session (distinct from a hard `failed_child` failure).
  - `phase_start` (~line 4254): same outbound-blocker gate for leaf items,
    placed **before** the Step 3 claim (so an unmet leaf blocker never leaves
    the item claimed `in_progress` with no worktree); refuse with the blocker
    list.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` (or a new
  `tests/test_implement_parent_outbound_gate.py`): regression cases per AC4,
  using the injectable runner pattern already used for the phase_parent tests
  (`fake_wl_dep_blockers` keyed by item id — extend to answer for the parent
  id too).
- `skill/implement/tests/`: regression case for the `phase_start` leaf gate
  (same target file family as `test_phase_start_claim.py`).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: Step 6.1 wording per AC5.
- **Ordering (test-first):** write the AC4 regression tests first, then the
  implementation gates (TDD, per the implement skill).

## Key files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `wl_dep_blockers` (~line 506; its
  only current call site is the child classification at line 5688),
  `phase_start` (~line 4254, claim at Step 3), `phase_parent` (~line 5569,
  child classification at Step 5), `phase_drive` (~line 6637, parent-report
  consumption)
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Step 6.1
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — phase_parent regression tests
  (injectable `wl_dep_blockers` runner); `skill/implement/tests/` for the
  `phase_start` gate case

## Assumptions (planning session, 2026-10-28)

- A1 — A parent with `status: blocked` and **no** outbound edges also gates
  starting (consistent with `wl next` skipping blocked items). The ACs phrase
  the requirement as blocked + unmet edge; honouring a plain `blocked` status
  is the safe default and is flagged for producer confirmation in the plan
  report.
- A2 — Machine-readable "blocked verdict": the parent report signals the
  blocked outcome via `parent_blocked_by` present, no `next_child`, no
  `parent_advanced`, with `success` kept true (soft stop mirroring the existing
  sibling-blocked path); `phase_drive` forwards `parent_blocked_by` so callers
  can distinguish `blocked` (soft) from `failed` (hard).
- A3 — The `phase_start` leaf gate sits before its claim step so a blocked leaf
  never ends up `in_progress` with no worktree.

## Related work

- SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J (open) — sibling gap in the same function (terminal
  blockers still gate topological readiness); complementary, not overlapping:
  that item fixes ordering over non-terminal in-chain blockers, this item gates
  starting on parent-level outbound blockers.
- SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T (completed) — introduced parent recursion with the
  "external blockers are coordination notes" assumption; that assumption needs
  the clarification in AC5.

## Notes

- The TCE item is **not** fixed by this item; it stays `blocked` until
  RISE-0MVN2V6YO002AHL4 lands, which is the correct end state — this item only
  makes the orchestrator honour that state.

## Plan: changelog (plan skill, 2026-10-28)

- AC bullets unwrapped to single lines (tooling parses each AC as one line).
- Key Files corrected: `skill/implement/tests/` → `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` (real phase_parent regression suite) + `skill/implement/tests/` for the start-gate case; line refs updated (phase_start ~4254, phase_parent ~5569, phase_drive ~6637, wl_dep_blockers ~506).
- Minimal implementation extended with gate placement (before Step 5 classification; before `phase_start` Step 3 claim), `phase_drive` `parent_blocked_by` forwarding, and test-first ordering.
- Assumptions A1–A3 recorded. No new child items created (S-sized, single-file change; coverage review: proceed, 100% covered).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (planning, 2026-10-28)

- No operator interview occurred (downtime dispatch). No clarifying questions were required to reach `plan_complete`.
- OPEN ITEM (directed to producer, non-blocking): confirm Assumption A1 — should a parent whose `status: blocked` has **no** outbound edges also refuse to start children? Recorded answer (plan, recommended default): yes, matched to `wl next` blocked-item semantics; the implementation options are scoped in A1/A2.

## Goal

Five tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` are source-code-grep / structural anti-patterns (per `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`). Rework them to assert observable behaviour, or delete them if the behaviour is already covered elsewhere. Discovered by the test-churn pruning review (analyser v2.1.0, dev @ 7875214).

## Affected tests (line numbers at discovery)

- L427 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents the audit gating step` — reads SKILL.md text, asserts word substrings.
- L462 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js imports checkAuditReadyToClose` — reads source text, asserts string presence (the import behaviour is already exercised by the module-import behaviour tests).
- L478 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js uses exit code 6 for audit gate failure` — reads source text, asserts `'return 6'`/similar. Behaviour should be verified by exercising run-release against a failing audit gate.
- L496 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents exit code 6 for audit gate` — includes a near-placeholder catch-all condition `(content.includes('6') && content.includes('audit'))` that matches almost any content.
- L865 `check-audit-gate: checkProducerReviewStatus has JSDoc comment` — structural-only test asserting documentation presence, not observable behaviour.

The file is otherwise healthy (89 tests, 255 asserts, real behaviour via `await import(MODULE_PATH)` + `execFileSync`); the fix must not remove the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The five tests above either pin observable behaviour (running the real module/gate and asserting output/exit codes) or are deleted.
- [ ] No test in the file reads a source or markdown file and asserts a substring of its text.
- [ ] The near-placeholder catch-all condition (L496) is eliminated.
- [ ] Behaviour previously pinned by each reworked test remains covered by a live test somewhere in the suite.
- [ ] Full suite passes after the change (run via the test skill).

## Goal

Users of the refactor skill need to know whether the project's **tests are
worth keeping**, not only whether the source has code smells. Integrate the
`test-churn` skill into the refactor workflow so every refactor run also
produces test-churn metrics (rewrite ratio, test growth, per-area churn), and
surface that evidence in the refactor skill's final report.

## Problem Statement

The refactor skill currently analyses **source code only** (`refactor.py` scans
`.py`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; tests are scanned for
smells like any other code, but their *value* is never assessed). Test-value
evidence exists but only on demand, via the separate `test-churn` skill
(`skill`-external, script `test_churn_analysis.py`). Nothing in the refactor
workflow detects a suite that is growing without manifest benefit, so the
`refactor` run cannot report the pruning signal documented in the test-churn
skill's pruning review workflow.

## User Stories

- **Agent running a refactor:** "When I run the refactor skill, the report tells
  me whether the test suite is growing without benefit, so I can file a
  pruning work item without remembering to run a second skill."
- **Operator / producer:** "Every refactor report carries reproducible test
  churn numbers, so TDD-ROI evidence is produced continuously rather than
  requested ad hoc."
- **Maintainer:** "The integration is additive — a missing/broken test-churn
  script never fails a refactor run, and `--no-churn` restores today's exact
  behaviour."

## Proposed Behaviour

1. `refactor.py` invokes the test-churn analyser as an **additional pipeline
   stage** after smell detection, for both invocation modes (full scan and
   session boundary).
2. A new `--no-churn` flag skips the stage (mirroring `--no-sync`,
   `--no-linter`, `--no-llm`) for offline/deterministic/fast runs.
3. The **human report** gains a test-churn section showing at minimum: modified
   only rewrite ratio, including-new rewrite ratio, net test lines/files
   growth, and the flagged top-churn areas.
4. The **`--json` report** gains a `test_churn` key carrying the analyser's
   `test_churn_data.json` payload (or a documented failure/omitted marker).
5. The stage is **non-fatal**: an unavailable analyser, non-git directory, or
   analyser error logs a warning and the refactor run continues with unchanged
   exit-code semantics (mirroring the existing `wl sync` policy).
6. `SKILL.md` documents the stage, the flag, the report section and the
   non-fatal policy, and cross-references the test-churn skill.

## Constraint: skill boundary

`skill/refactor/` must not import `test_churn_analysis.py` from the installed
skill directory. The integration must resolve the analyser at runtime (the
documented `$(skill_path test-churn)` pattern) or invoke it as a subprocess, so
this repo stays the canonical source and no copy of the analyser is vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A full-project `/skill:refactor` run renders a test-churn section in the human report containing the modified-only rewrite ratio, the including-new rewrite ratio, and net test line growth.
- [ ] AC2: `refactor.py --json` emits a `test_churn` key whose value contains the analyser metrics (at minimum the two rewrite ratios and `growth_metrics`).
- [ ] AC3: `--no-churn` skips the stage and produces a report byte-identical to current behaviour (no test-churn section, no `test_churn` key).
- [ ] AC4: When the analyser is unavailable or returns non-zero, the run logs a warning, completes successfully, and reports the stage as unavailable — the refactor exit code is unchanged.
- [ ] AC5: `session boundary` mode (`refactor.py <work-item-id>`) also runs the stage, and its work-item `StatusLifecycle` behaviour is unchanged (item never left `in_progress`).
- [ ] AC6: New tests cover the added stage (report rendering, JSON key, `--no-churn`, and the non-fatal failure path) without shelling out to the real analyser — following the test-writing guidelines (no source-grep or self-referential tests).
- [ ] AC7: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` documents the stage, flag, report section, non-fatal policy and the cross-reference to the test-churn skill.
- [ ] AC8: No code under `skill/refactor/` imports from an installed skill path; the analyser is resolved at runtime or invoked as a subprocess.
- [ ] AC9: Full suite passes (run via the test skill).
data.title: Integrate test-churn analysis into the refactor skill and report

## Goal

Make the project's test suite **earn its runtime**: every remaining test should
pin observable behaviour, and no test should exist that cannot fail for a
reason a developer cares about. This epic covers a complete, evidence-led
test-value refactor of the suite — measure, classify, prune, rework, and guard
against reintroduction — rather than the current one-file-at-a-time ad-hoc
cleanups.

## Problem Statement

The suite has grown substantially and carries demonstrable waste:

- **Measured growth (test-churn analyser v2.1.0, `dev` @ 7875214):**
  208,809 test lines added vs 71,787 deleted → **net +137,022 lines**;
  498 test files added vs 114 deleted → **net +384 files**. Net growth is
  positive in **every** calendar quarter, accelerating in 2026-Q3 (+55,892)
  and 2026-Q4 (+38,024).
- **Rewrite ratio is LOW** (14.0% modified-only, 6.2% including new files),
  which means tests largely *survive* feature evolution. That is good news for
  TDD value, but it means growth is dominated by **additive accumulation**,
  not churn — precisely the pattern where dead, duplicated and
  source-grep/structural tests survive unnoticed because nothing forces them
  to be re-examined.
- **Known confirmed offenders found so far:** 5 source-grep / structural
  anti-pattern tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
  (SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23); 15 test helpers invoking real `git` non-hermetically
  (already tracked, SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0).
- There is **no standing mechanism** that classifies test files by value, so
  every finding so far depended on a human/agent choosing to look.

## Why an epic (not another leaf)

Value assessment is a repeatable pipeline — detect candidates, prove they no
longer map to behaviour, prune or rework, verify nothing broke, and prevent
reintroduction. That needs coordinated child items across measurement,
classification, remediation, and guarding; single-file items cannot deliver it.

## Existing related work — do NOT duplicate

These items already exist and must be **depended on / coordinated with**, not
recreated:

- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — rework the 5 source-grep tests in `test-check-audit-gate.mjs`.
- `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0` — migrate 15 raw-git test helpers to `git_sandbox` (hermeticity, not value).
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled test-churn runs across projects.

## Scope

1. **Measure (baseline).** Capture the test-churn baseline (rewrite ratios, net
   growth, per-area churn, suite wall-clock runtime, per-file runtime) so every
   later change is provable.
2. **Classify.** Run the code-path evaluator (`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`)
   plus the `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern checklist
   over the whole suite, recording a **keep / rework / prune** verdict per file.
3. **Prove.** For each prune candidate, demonstrate the behaviour it pins is
   either not observable, already covered elsewhere, or no longer exists
   (`git blame` + coverage grep of the public API). Mutation testing is the
   tie-breaker where provenance is unclear.
4. **Remediate.** Prune dead/duplicate tests; rework devalued ones (source-grep
   → behaviour; placeholder → real assertion or delete; simulation → exercise
   production code).
5. **Guard.** Add a regression guard so the pruned anti-pattern classes cannot
   be reintroduced silently, and so future additions are screened.
6. **Report.** Record before/after metrics so the value delivered is auditable.

## Non-goals

- Not a coverage-maximisation exercise: reducing test count is acceptable and
  expected where tests pin nothing.
- Not a rewrite of the audit/refactor/implement skills' behaviour.
- Not the hermeticity migration (tracked separately in `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A baseline is recorded in this item: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, and the evaluator/checklist verdict for every test file in scope.
- [ ] AC2: Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] AC3: Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] AC4: All `prune`-verdict tests are removed and all `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text.
- [ ] AC5: After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] AC6: The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] AC7: Suite wall-clock runtime is measurably reduced (or, where runtime rises, the item documents why the surviving tests justify it) with before/after numbers.
- [ ] AC8: A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] AC9: The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] AC10: Full project test suite passes with the changes, and the final report records the before/after deltas.

## Risks

- **Removing a useful test is a regression; keeping a dead one only costs
  runtime.** Pruning criteria stay conservative — when in doubt, keep the test
  and file a work item.
- Deleting tests can raise apparent coverage drops: coverage is judged by
  behaviour/AC mapping (AC6), never by percentage alone.
- Suite-wide classification is expensive; it must be batched with bounded
  fan-out per the test execution policy (never ad-hoc full suites).

## Notes

Discovered during a test-churn pruning review, 2026-10-28. Priority is medium
because the measured rewrite ratio is already LOW (tests largely survive
feature evolution) — the waste here is accumulation, not thrash, so this is
valuable hygiene rather than an emergency. Children to be created at plan
stage.
data.title: Complete test-value refactor: ensure every test earns its runtime
