## Summary

The assignee-hold convention (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`: "non-empty assignee = scheduling hold (producer `Map`; clear to release)") makes a lingering agent assignee a dispatch blocker: a held item is invisible to `wl next` and cannot be re-picked. Clear-on-terminal has so far been implemented **piecemeal**, per skill:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` + `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — clear the assignee on every terminal outcome (SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — clears the assignee on every terminal verdict (SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS, SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5).

There is **no systemic guarantee**. `StatusLifecycle.clear_assignee_on_exit` deliberately defaults to `False` ("no silent behaviour change"), so every new or un-audited skill/script that claims with an `assignee` silently re-introduces the hold. This item makes assignee release on terminal outcomes the default, enforced invariant rather than a per-caller opt-in.

## Gap (current state)

Code paths that set a non-empty assignee today:

| Path | Terminal release | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_start`, `phase_finish`, `phase_abort`, `phase_parent`, drive stranded-child finalise, signal safety reset) | yes | covered by SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM |
| `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` (`cmd_start`/`cmd_finish`/`cmd_auto_complete`/`cmd_abort` + failure resets) | yes | covered by SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM |
| `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (claim + all terminal verdict paths) | yes | covered by SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS / SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5 |
| `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` `StatusLifecycle` | **opt-in only** | `clear_assignee_on_exit` default `False`; failure branch clears only when constructed with `assignee=` |
| `skill/plan/SKILL.md` claim pattern | n/a (claims `in_progress` with **no** assignee) | invariant is documented but not asserted |
| `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` (creates rec items with `--assignee`) | n/a (intentional producer hold on creation) | must not be regressed by this change |
| `skill/audit/scripts/verify_context_reduction.py` | restores a pre-existing assignee | must not be regressed by this change |

Also unverified: dispatcher/downtime-dispatch paths (herdr worker `phase_*`/`drive` wrappers) that claim a child and may be terminated by timeout or signal — a claim left behind by a killed session is the highest-frequency real-world hold.

## User Story

As a producer/dispatcher, I need every skill and helper that claims a work item with an assignee to release that assignee on every terminal outcome (success, failure, abort, timeout, signal) **by default**, so no completed or abandoned item is ever left on a scheduling hold that blocks re-dispatch.

## Desired Change

1. **Make release the default in the shared helper.** `StatusLifecycle` clears the assignee on every exit path (success, failure, restore) **unless** the caller explicitly opts out (`preserve_assignee_on_exit=True`, or an equivalent documented escape hatch). Audit every existing caller so no legacy behaviour changes silently — any caller that must keep the assignee (producer holds, `verify_context_reduction` restore) opts out explicitly and says why in a comment.
2. **Cover non-`StatusLifecycle` paths.** The signal/timeout safety resets and the dispatcher-facing `phase_*` / `drive` entry points must release the assignee even when the process is killed (already partly done in `implement.py`; verify and extend where needed).
3. **Inventory and regression-proof it.** A single table-driven regression test enumerating every skill's terminal entry point, asserting `assignee == ""` after both a success and a failure/abort exit. New skills must be added to that table — the test is the enforcement point.
4. **Document the invariant.** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (or the linked skill docs) state: "any code path that claims an `assignee` must release it on every terminal outcome; a persistent hold is represented by the producer assignee (`Map`) or `needsProducerReview`, never by a lingering agent assignee."

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — flip the default, add the explicit opt-out, update the module docstring/table.
- `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py` — success/failure/restore default-clear assertions; opt-out pinning.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — drop now-redundant per-call `clear_assignee_on_exit=True` / add explicit opt-outs where a hold is intentional.
- `skill/audit/scripts/verify_context_reduction.py` — explicit preserve/restore opt-out.
- New/extended cross-skill test (e.g. `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py`) — the table-driven terminal-path matrix.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — invariant wording.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A written inventory (in this item) of every code path that sets a non-empty assignee, each classified as *must release on terminal* or *intentional hold* with a one-line justification
- [ ] `StatusLifecycle` releases the assignee on every exit path (success, failure, restore) **by default**; preserving it requires an explicit, documented opt-out
- [ ] Every existing caller is audited; any caller relying on the old default is either updated or given an explicit opt-out with an inline comment explaining why
- [ ] Intentional holds are unaffected: producer-assignee holds (`Map`), `needsProducerReview` holds, `agent-log-review` creation assignees, and `verify_context_reduction`'s assignee restore all behave exactly as before (pinned by tests)
- [ ] A table-driven regression test asserts `assignee == ""` after both success and failure/abort for every skill terminal entry point (implement, intake, audit, plan, and any dispatcher-facing `phase_*`/`drive` finaliser), and fails loudly when a new skill is missing from the table
- [ ] Signal/timeout kill paths release the assignee (verified by test, not just by inspection)
- [ ] The invariant is documented once (canonical wording) with the skill `SKILL.md` files cross-referencing it
- [ ] Full project test suite passes at the dev-push gate

## Constraints

- No new external dependencies.
- Must not weaken the assignee-hold convention itself: a producer's hold must still block dispatch.
- The audit tier's status-neutral claim (`--if-assignee ""`, staying `completed`/`in_review`) must keep working unchanged.
- Behaviour changes must be observable in tests, not just prose — no silent semantic change without a pinning test.
- UK English in all docs.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: flipping a shared default is a wide blast radius.** Mitigation: the caller audit + table-driven matrix land in the same change; every caller is either updated or explicitly opted out.
- **Risk: a killed process cannot run Python exit hooks.** Mitigation: release must be persisted on the last durable write where possible, plus a stale-hold sweep (see below) rather than relying solely on `finally`.
- **Risk: masking genuine failures.** A release must never hide an error — logging of the terminal outcome is preserved.
- **Assumption:** "finished" means any terminal outcome — success (`completed`/`in_review`), failure (`open`), abort, timeout, or signal.
- **Out of scope (candidate follow-up):** a TTL-based stale-hold reaper for holds left by processes that die without any exit path (ContextHub precedent: SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E). File separately if the signal-path tests show it is still reachable.

## Related Work

- **implement/intake: clear assignee on completion regardless of outcome (SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM)** — completed/in_review; established the `clear_assignee_on_exit` opt-in and the implement/intake behaviour.
- **Audit runner: clear assignee on terminal verdicts and keep review-queue items completed/in_review (SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS)** — done; audit-tier precedent.
- **Audit runner: set needsProducerReview on 'yes' verdicts ... keep assignee clear-on-terminal (SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5)** — done; documents the hold-via-`needsProducerReview` alternative to a lingering assignee.
- **AGENTS_GLOBAL.md claim pattern: status-neutral assignee CAS + assignee-hold convention (SA-0MVA79DNT001HQBB)** — done; defines the convention this item enforces.
- **Shared status lifecycle helper for skills (SA-0MRW7ER4L000SK8Z)** — done; the helper whose default this item changes.
- **Always mark items as in_progress while an agent is working on them (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9)** — done; the complementary claim invariant.
- **TTL-bounded monotonic claim-hold guard (SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E)** — done (ContextHub); precedent for the bounded-stale-hold follow-up noted above.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required — the seed description already carries a testable goal, a gap inventory, measurable acceptance criteria, constraints, and a related-work report. Intake was auto-completed.

- **Q (implicit):** Which of the existing per-skill items already cover this work? — **Answer (agent research):** none covers the systemic default. `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` still defaults `clear_assignee_on_exit=False`; `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` clears the assignee explicitly on each terminal path (`cmd_finish`/`cmd_auto_complete`/`cmd_abort` + failure resets); `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:6354` is the sole `clear_assignee_on_exit=True` caller. Source: repo grep + `git log` (SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM only ever touched implement/intake).
- **Q (implicit):** Is the issue type correct? — **Answer (agent):** `task` retained — cross-cutting refactor + tests + documentation, no net-new end-user capability and nothing currently "broken" in a user-visible way.
- **Assumption recorded:** "terminal outcome" includes success (`completed`/`in_review`), failure (`open`), abort, timeout, and signal; a kill with no Python exit hook is addressed by persisted-on-last-durable-write plus the TTL stale-hold reaper filed as out-of-scope follow-up.
- **Open question (non-blocking, for the implementer):** whether the table-driven cross-skill regression test lives under `skill/shared/` or a top-level `tests/` directory — decide by matching where the existing cross-skill tests sit at implementation time.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MV9DUE6F006SK1H** – Ship release gate re-homed onto the producer assignee hold (from WL-0MV85WESL002SD0F) (completed)
- **SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS** – Audit runner: clear assignee on terminal verdicts and keep review-queue items completed/in_review (from WL-0MV85WE7Q00044P9) (completed)
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** – implement skill: /skill:implement <parent-id> must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: abort, acceptance, add, added, agent (+310 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: abort, acceptance, add, added, agent (+302 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abandoned, abort, add, added, agent (+294 more)

# Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks above a shebang or encoding line

**Headline:** `inject_refactor_comment()` unconditionally prepends its marker
block, so on any file that opens with `#!/usr/bin/env python3` (or a PEP 263
encoding line) the injected comment lands above the interpreter directive. The
resulting file is no longer directly executable and ruff reports `EXE005`
("Shebang should be at the beginning of the file") — a formatting finding filed
*against the file the skill just annotated*, which then spawns a fresh
low-priority refactor work item that only undoes the skill's own edit.

## Problem statement

`skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` builds a marker block and writes
`new_content = comment_block + original_content`. For executable scripts this
breaks the shebang contract and creates a self-sustaining loop: the skill
injects a marker → the next refactor run's linter sees `EXE005` → a new work
item is filed → the fix deletes the marker → the next refactor run injects it
again.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement
  pipeline's refactor step — they inherit preventable lint findings and
  executable-bit regressions on files the skill touched.
- **Producers triaging the refactor backlog** — self-inflicted, duplicate items
  consume triage and implementation capacity.
- **Developers** — annotated scripts must stay directly runnable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inject_refactor_comment()` inserts its block *after* any shebang
      (`#!…`) and any PEP 263 coding line, and after a Python module docstring
      when the file opens with one; on files with none of these the block still
      goes to the top as today.
- [ ] Markdown/HTML block-style markers (`<!-- … -->`) keep their current
      placement behaviour, except that a leading shebang or coding line in a
      non-Markdown file is never displaced.
- [ ] Line endings and trailing newline state are preserved (write with
      `newline=""`), so the fix does not normalise CRLF files.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` cover: a file
      starting with a shebang, a file with shebang + coding line, a file with
      shebang + docstring, a plain Python file with no shebang, and a Markdown
      file — each asserting shebang stays on line 1.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that running the repository's lint gate over a
      file annotated by the skill reports no `EXE005`/`EXE001`-style executable
      findings.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (the "REFACTOR Comments"
      section), and any relevant docs entries.

## Constraints

- Do **not** change marker syntax, the duplicate-suppression match on smell
  type, or `get_comment_style()` file-type mapping — placement only.
- Removal of stale markers on work-item close is **out of scope**; that is
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`.
- Keep the change confined to `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` and its
  tests.

## Existing state

```python
# skill/refactor/comment_injection.py
    # Place comment at the top of the file
    new_content = comment_block + original_content
```

`_build_comment_block()` prefixes the block with `"
"` unconditionally, so even
a token ending in a newline gains an extra blank line above the shebang.

Evidence from the field: on 2026-10-30 the implement pipeline's refactor step
annotated `src/rss_server.py` in the ContentCreator project, pushing
`#!/usr/bin/env python3` from line 1 to line 13 and producing
`EXE005 Shebang should be at the beginning of the file`. The finding was filed
as `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0`, implemented as removing the skill's own marker, and
pinned with `tests/test_rss_script_entrypoint.py`.

## Desired change

`inject_refactor_comment()` computes an insertion offset from the file head
(shebang, then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splices the
block there, leaving the file head byte-identical otherwise.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — compute insertion offset; write with
  `newline=""`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — placement tests for the
  shebang / coding-line / docstring / Markdown cases
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — state the placement rule in the "REFACTOR
  Comments" section

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a marker placed after the module docstring is still found by
  `has_existing_comment()`, which scans the whole file rather than the head.
- **Risk (low):** docstring detection is heuristic; an over-eager match could
  move the marker into the middle of code. Mitigation: match only a leading
  triple-quoted string that terminates before the first statement, and fall back
  to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "annotation lifecycle" refactor (placement,
  removal, sweep) is tempting. Record such work against
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` instead of widening this item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` — remove stale `REFACTOR-` markers when their work item
  closes (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — the ContentCreator item that this defect created
  (fixed by deleting the marker and pinning the entrypoint contract).
- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — the ContentCreator sweep of stale markers left in
  tests and scripts.

data.comment:
Implementation (working-tree attribution for the live-repo guard) — commit `ae5258ef9`.

**Q1 assumption (documented per AGENTS.md).** Appendix Q1 was still unanswered, so the plan's **recommended option (a) — pre-existing-dirty attribution** was implemented exactly as sized (S). Option (c) isolated execution would have required a re-plan (L) and was not attempted.

**Rule adopted (git plumbing only — never a `wl-*`/path-name pattern, AC4).** Provenance is the start snapshot's own `git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` map:
- status entry **present at start, absent at end** → the path was *resolved* inside the guard window → **excluded** from the verdict, reported as a note (AC1/AC3). A hermetic suite never commits/checks out/reverts, so this is concurrent churn.
- status entry **absent at start, present at end** (modified / deleted / newly created) → **mutation** (AC2, the retained clean→dirty direction).
- status entry present at both with a **different code** → **mutation** (no resolution is observable, so nothing is attributable). This keeps the excluded class as narrow as the observed incident.

**Note format (AC3).** `excluded: concurrently resolved working-tree change in <checkout>: <path> [<code>]`, carried as `live_repo_excluded` (list) in the `run_tests.py` JSON result, printed as `note:` lines in text output, printed by the inner plugin at session end, and logged/recorded by `implement.py finish` (`Live-repo guard note: …` + `report["live_repo_excluded"]`).

**Files changed.** `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (attribution + `excluded_working_tree_churn`/`excluded_churn_notes`, module docstring incl. blind spots), `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`_detect_live_repo_mutation` now returns `{"mutation", "excluded"}`; `guarded_run_all` emits `live_repo_excluded`; CLI prints `note:`), `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` (accumulates + prints notes, re-baseline-safe), `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (carry-through + finish-gate log/report), docs (`docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.1/§8.4/§8.5, `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`).

**Tests (TDD, helper first).** `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`: `TestWorkingTreeAttribution` (benign concurrent commit of a pre-dirty tracked path and of a pre-dirty `??` path, performed by a second actor in a hermetic `git_sandbox` repo; helper-level parity), `TestWorkingTreeAttributionIncidents` (modify/delete/create from a clean start still mutate; a `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*`-shaped newly created path still mutates — the rule is not name-based), `TestWorkingTreeAttributionBoundaries` (pinned blind spots: masked revert, masked delete of a pre-existing untracked file, still-dirty-different-code stays a mutation, invisible content-only change). Guard-level parity: `TestWorkingTreeAttributionNested` (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`), outer-guard `live_repo_excluded` e2e + verdict tests (`skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`), and finish-gate carry-through (`skill/implement/tests/test_implement_guard_ownership.py`).

**AC5 (recorded evidence, no re-implementation).** On `dev` @ `ae5258ef9`: `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT = "refs/heads/dev"` and `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES = ("refs/remotes/origin/",)` in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`; `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand = 2700`; `implement.py _resolve_test_timeout()` reads `timeoutPerCommand` with a 600 s default.

**Gate evidence.** Changed-scope validation green (pytest, exit 0, 1361 s) before commit `ae5258ef9`; the full suite is enforced at the dev-push gate. The first push attempt was aborted by a remote-host connection drop (not a test failure); a manual push is in progress at the time of writing.

Cross-repo evidence for why this is now user-visible and higher-value than when filed (2026-10-25).

## The parity consumer has already moved to schema 2

ContextHub `wl` upgraded its read-path fingerprint port to exactly the schema this item specifies — `ContextHub/src/audit-fingerprint.ts` `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2`, payload `{"schema": 2, "title_hash", "description_hash"}`, zero git calls — on 2026-10-23 (WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7, commit `213a96b7`). `wl list` / `wl worklist` / review-queue grouping now compute `currentFingerprint` with it and compare it to the stored fingerprint under `isAuditFresh` (`ContextHub/packages/shared/src/icons.ts:457` — a bare string compare).

## The installed skill is still pre-v2, and the skew is silent

The installed audit skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, identical to this repo's `skill/audit` at `fe85415a3`) has **no** `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` constant and still hashes `json.dumps({path_states, description_hash, key_files})` (~lines 2477-2485). Because the payloads differ, the digests can never be equal, so **every audit persisted since 2026-10-23 05:14 renders as out-of-date** in every `isAuditFresh`-driven view.

Observed today on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (llm project, "False 'saturated' capacity signal starves herdr downtime dispatcher overnight"):

- stored fingerprint `ecf5ccd420f9d5c18f8d61eb6d27dca0af8bcd597dd98b9349f8d30ac6f3df22` — reproduced **exactly** by `audit_runner._compute_content_fingerprint` run right now against the current item;
- `wl list` `currentFingerprint` `bd0d5f10a8ff051ce0bff653f27205107d5068805294006bad46f5b0d37006b5`;
- audit content itself is fine: 4/4 ACs `met`, merge gate verified, "Ready to close: Yes".

The drift shipped green because ContextHub's parity guard `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` classifies **any** schema skew ("ahead or behind") as a *skip* that merely names the installed schema — tracked as **WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y** ("Audit fingerprint parity skew must never be silent"), which makes skew a hard failure plus a `wl doctor` warning.

## Additional acceptance criteria for this item

- AC (new): after landing, the installed helper must expose `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2` and accept the documented call signature so `ContextHub/tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` performs a **real** byte-for-byte digest comparison instead of a skew skip; a parity run against ContextHub must pass (verification step for AC6).

WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y hard-fails on a pre-v2 installed skill, so it is deliberately sequenced **after** this item ships and is reinstalled. Cross-store dependency edges are not expressible with `wl dep`; the ordering is recorded in both items.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## F2 root cause — the disk-reading parity false pass is a verdict-provenance failure (a verdict from a different tree), not untracked-file invisibility

Pinned by **SA-0MVQHV8JE007MAK3** (F2). Reproduced at the finish-gate entry point with a hermetic fixture; no real worklog, main checkout or network.

### Named mechanism

**Stale/foreign cache entry whose fingerprint belongs to a different tree** (the "verdict may not correspond to a suite run at the gate's tree" branch of the parent investigation). Two facts combine:

1. `test_cache.compute_git_state` fingerprints `HEAD` plus the content of every path `git status` reports. Generated metadata — the wiki registry in question — is gitignored, so it is **invisible** to the fingerprint. The key also carries no checkout identity.
2. Consequently two on-disk trees that differ only in generated metadata share one cache key. A green full-suite run recorded for the rebuilt-metadata tree is served, within TTL, for the lagging-metadata tree. The gate then reports green for a tree whose parity suite is red on disk, and no field in the verdict says which tree ran or whether it was cache-served.

Untracked-file invisibility (F1, SA-0MVQHV72U003UJUB) provably cannot explain this case: `test_registry_documents_match_on_disk_documents` never asks git — it reads the registry and the document set off disk — so staging the change set changes nothing for it. A green verdict for that red tree therefore cannot have been produced by the gate's own tree: it was produced for a different tree (wrong checkout / shared-cache collision / metadata lag), which is exactly the mechanism captured here.

### Evidence trail (origin record OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA, OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2)

- 08:53 green full-suite entry in the shared `.worklog/cache`, state `8e9c3ea7…`, **2751** tests collected — the dev tree *before* the episode work's test files existed.
- 10:56 red run, state `f73d063e…`, **2781** tests — the committed tree.
- The gate's own per-worktree cache entry was deleted with the worktree, so the exact entry it served is unrecoverable; the surviving shared entry shows a pre-change tree's green run sitting in the cache the gate consults (causal argument accepted by the operator, plan Q2=a).
- Test-count asymmetry (2751 vs 2781) rules out "the same tree ran": the green entry collected a smaller tree than the commit contained.

### Reproduction (hermetic, gate entry point)

`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py`:

- `test_parity_verdict_reflects_the_gate_tree_when_the_suite_genuinely_runs` — with no cached entry the gate runs the parity suite against its own tree and reports red, naming `test_registry_documents_match_on_disk_documents`. Proves the fixture is a real parity detector and the verdict follows the tree that ran.
- `test_baseline_capture_parity_false_pass_from_a_foreign_cache_entry` — **the reproduction**: a *real* green run recorded against the rebuilt-metadata tree is served for the lagging-metadata tree (the two states are asserted fingerprint-identical), the gate reports `{"scope": "full", "success": true}`, the cache entry's `completed_at` is unchanged (served, not produced), while the same tree's suite is red the moment it runs.
- `test_parity_foreign_cache_entry_misses_once_f7_lands` — strict `xfail` (tracer-bullet convention used by F1): after F7 the entry must miss and the suite re-run red, with the parity test named; the entry's fingerprint (`compute_git_state` over the loose tree) is asserted to differ from `git write-tree` over the staged would-be-commit tree. Verified to fail today at exactly that assertion (not at setup).
- `tests/test_test_cache.py::test_generated_metadata_is_invisible_to_the_git_state_fingerprint` — cache-layer pin: rebuilding gitignored generated metadata never moves the key, so a green verdict from a different on-disk tree is served (one execution only).

### Consequence for the parent fix

- **F7 (SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB) is the necessary and sufficient closure for the parity case**: binding cache acceptance to the would-be-commit tree fingerprint (`git write-tree` over the staged index, operator option A) makes a loose-fingerprint entry a miss and forces a re-run. The F6 temp index alone does not close it — staging does not change what an on-disk parity suite reads — which is why the parity case and the tracked-file case need both children.
- Legacy/provenance-less entries must fail closed (plan Q3=a) so a carried-over entry cannot be served as the gate's green.
- The gate's classified minimum here is a verdict that names the tree and whether it was cache-served (F8), so this mechanism can never again be silent.

**Cross-repo coverage note — mid-run checkout drift (AI_Hell AH-0MVSRO0MM004T450, closed as covered by this family per producer Q1 = c).**

Please confirm this umbrella (or one of its children) covers the *start≠end state drift* dimension, not only "which tree should have been tested":

**Observed defect (AI_Hell, 2026-10-28):** a full-suite run in the main checkout fast-forwarded from `4d9daf0b` to `c1330ef3` 69 s into a 150 s run. The run loaded a post-checkout test file against a pre-checkout source module (shared integration worker had already transformed it) and reported 6 failures for a state that never existed at any commit; the triage helper then minted a critical `test-failure` item (AH-0MVSPXLIN0000P1R, since completed as not reproducible). Evidence: `.worklog/cache/bcf7b83c…` (red, exit 1) vs `.worklog/cache/e13cbd7ab82128fb5d8c19f1aeb4da67` (green, same tree) in AI_Hell.

**Why it is not obviously covered by the current child contracts:** `skill/test_cache.py:run_cached()` fingerprints the git state **once, before** execution and calls `store(..., git_state=<pre-run fingerprint>)` when the runner returns — so a drifted run is stored *under the pre-run state* and can be served as evidence for it. Tree-fingerprint binding (SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB) fixes *which* fingerprint keys the entry, but a run that starts and ends at different trees still has a single pre-computed key. Likewise `guarded_run_all`'s `live_repo_mutation` is detect-only: `implement.py:_gate_failure_kind()` classifies parseable failures as `test_failure` first, and `audit_runner.py:_run_suite_and_triage()` (F3, unguarded) calls `check_or_create()` per parsed failure.

**Suggested coverage (if not already planned):** a post-run `compute_git_state()` comparison in `run_cached`; on mismatch write no cache entry under either fingerprint, emit `state_changed_during_run` with no failure records, and classify it as infrastructure (implement gate) / skip triage (audit F3). data.author: plan
data.comment:
## Plan: pane-per-child drive transport (4 child slices)

Transport decision taken from the intake Appendix: **option B** — an interactive
Pi TUI agent per child in a sibling pane of the calling tab, driven by
`herdr pane split` + `agent start/prompt/wait` + `pane close`, with
`phase_parent`'s work-item stage as the authoritative completion signal.
Headless `pi -p` remains the default outside Herdr.

### Feature slices (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Child | Slice | Covers parent AC |
|---|-------|-------|------------------|
| 1 | SA-0MVPHXNTJ006TNFB — Herdr session helper and fake CLI | Shared fail-open session-level Herdr boundary + recording fake CLI (test foundation) | AC1 (helper half) |
| 2 | SA-0MVPHYIIE002OBC8 — Pane session spawner and opt-in transport | `_pane_session_spawner`, detection + opt-in selection, env isolation, focus flag | AC1, AC5, AC6, AC8 |
| 3 | SA-0MVPHZ1CI0045QR0 — Drive pane lifecycle and report parity | done/blocked/timeout lifecycle, close-or-retain, `pane_id`/`transport` report parity | AC2, AC3, AC4, AC7, AC9 |
| 4 | SA-0MVPHZJ22007L8LQ — Document pane-driven sessions | Reference doc + SKILL.md Step 6.1 operator docs and worked example | AC10 |

Dependency edges: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 (`wl dep`), so `drive` runs them serially in
this order. AC11 (build/tests/full-suite gate) is restated on every child.

### Vertical-slice and test-first rationale

Each slice ships code + tests + docs for its own surface (no horizontal
"all tests" phase). Test-first ordering is satisfied **within** each slice and
by making slice 1 a test-foundation deliverable (fake Herdr CLI + fixtures +
contract assertions) that blocks every implementation slice. Committing
standalone red tests is not possible: the commit gate requires
build → test → commit with a green changed scope, so a separate "write failing
tests" work item would violate it.

### Decisions recorded (no producer question needed)

- **Herdr CLI boundary location** (intake Appendix forked-decision): keep it in
  `skill/shared/`, extending `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`'s conventions
  (`HERDR_BIN_PATH` resolution, subprocess env, fail-open return style) rather
  than duplicating resolution logic in `implement.py`. The intake brief already
  states this preference, so it is applied rather than raised as a question.
- **Spawner result shape**: `_pane_session_spawner` returns a superset of
  `_default_session_spawner`'s `{"success","returncode","reason"}` plus
  `pane_id`/`transport`, so `phase_drive`'s existing failure reconciliation
  (`_reconcile_spawn_failure`, `completed-late`, stranded detection) is reused
  unchanged.
- **Completion authority**: `phase_parent` stage re-read stays authoritative;
  `agent wait --until done|blocked` is a fast-path/stop signal only (parent AC2).
- **Pane hygiene**: close on confirmed-terminal success or timeout; retain (and
  report, with an `⚠️`/`🚫` pane title) on blocked/failed — never leak silently.

### Coordination note

`SA-0MVOABYW00004978` (Prevent duplicate drive child sessions — exclusive
per-child lock) also edits the `phase_drive` loop. It is still `open`/
`intake_complete`; the slices here touch the spawner selection and reporting
paths, not the child-lock logic, so no dependency edge was added. Rebase/review
awareness needed if it lands first.

### Automated review stages

1. Requirements & AC alignment review — all 11 parent ACs trace to exactly one
   child slice (`compute_coverage`: 100%); no invented or contradictory ACs;
   constraints (`agent_not_ready`, CLI API drift, no repo-external edits) are
   carried into slice notes.
2. Completeness review — every child has Goal, ACs, Implementation notes,
   `**Key Files:**` (validated with `validate_key_files_format()`), Dependencies
   and Deliverables.
3. Sequencing & dependencies review — dependency chain matches the test-first
   order (test foundation → spawner → lifecycle → docs).
4. Scope sizing review — four deliverable increments, each independently
   shippable with its own tests and docs; no slice spans more than one transport
   concern.
5. Acceptance & testability review — ACs are pass/fail via fake-CLI assertions,
   report-field assertions and doc review; timeout semantics expressed as the
   existing bounded-wait behaviour.
6. Polish & handoff review — descriptions are copy-pasteable for
   `/skill:implement <child>` with explicit key files and no unstated
   prerequisites.
7. AC coverage review — `apply_coverage_review` → `proceed`, coverage 100%,
   stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Does planning need to resurface the intake forked-decision (herdr CLI
  boundary in `skill/shared/` vs local to `implement.py`) to the producer?"
  Answer (plan agent): No — the intake Appendix already records the preference
  ("prefer reuse of `herdr_pane.py`'s resolution/fail-open conventions either
  way"), so the decision is applied as `skill/shared/` extension rather than a
  blocking question. Evidence: intake brief, "Appendix: decisions from the
  discovery conversation".
- Q: "Should a standalone 'write failing tests first' work item be created to
  satisfy test-first ordering?" Answer (plan agent): No — the commit gate
  requires build → test → commit with green changed scope, so red tests cannot
  be committed. Test-first ordering is instead expressed by making slice 1 the
  test foundation (fake Herdr CLI + fixtures + contract assertions) that blocks
  all implementation slices. Evidence: `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` commit gate,
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
- Q: "Should slice 1 and slice 2 be merged into one child?" Answer (plan agent):
  No — the shared helper is independently testable and reusable outside
  `implement.py` (slice 1), while the spawner/opt-in selection is specific to
  drive (slice 2); merging would make one oversized slice with two failure
  surfaces. Evidence: intake "Design sketch" bullets 1-2.
- Q: "Does `SA-0MVOABYW00004978` (per-child drive lock) block these slices?"
  Answer (plan agent): No dependency edge — it targets child-lock
  serialisation, which this plan does not modify; recorded as a coordination
  note above. Evidence: `wl show SA-0MVOABYW00004978`.

No OPEN QUESTIONs remain; no producer input required to implement.

data.comment:
Implementation complete (pending finish gate).

## What changed
- **New `skill/refactor/path_filters.py`** — canonical scan-scope module: `filter_scannable_paths(paths, repo_root, config, ...)`, `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRS` (extended with node_modules, vendor, third_party, third-party, site-packages, bower_components, jspm_packages, packages), `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS`, `has_source_extension`, `is_excluded_path`, `matches_patterns`, `extract_path_filters`.
- **`skill/refactor/session_boundary.py`** — `_EXCLUDED_DIRS` / `_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` now sourced from path_filters (extended set); `_is_source_file` uses the shared predicates, which also fixes the previously dead `*.egg-info` glob entry (it was compared literally).
- **`skill/refactor/scripts/config.py`** — `RefactorConfig.path_exclude` / `path_include` parsed from `exclude` / `include`, tolerant of malformed values (`_as_str_list`), serialised by `to_dict()`.
- **`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py`** — `detect_session_files(parent_branch, full_project, config, repo_root)` filters once per branch (full-project: extension + defaults + config + gitignore; session: same minus the extension check so non-source changes are still reported). `refactor_pipeline` threads the loaded config through. `_load_config` now also discovers `.refactor.json` in the project root (previously only `--config` was honoured) and returns default-rules-merged config via `load_rules`.
- **Tests** — new `tests/test_refactor/test_path_filters.py` (29 tests, AC1–AC7): real temp git repos for the gitignore cases, batch-call counting, graceful degradation, config precedence, session filtering and report counts.
- **Docs** — `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/refactor.md`, `.refactor.json.example` document the default exclusions, `.gitignore` behaviour (tracked files too, single batched call), `exclude`/`include` keys and precedence, and the `packages/` re-include note.

## Decisions / assumptions
1. **include beats everything** (defaults, config exclude, *and* .gitignore) for matched paths — an explicit re-include must not be silently defeated by a .gitignore rule. Documented under 'Filter precedence'.
2. **Session scans do not apply the source-extension check** — only exclusions. Keeps existing behaviour of reporting every touched file (e.g. `docs/notes.md`) while stopping external code from reaching auto-fix/detection.
3. **`.refactor.json` auto-discovery added** in `_load_config` — without it the documented 'create .refactor.json in project root' path had no effect (only `--config` was read). No config file present ⇒ identical behaviour to before.
4. **Single batch gitignore call** — one `git check-ignore --no-index --stdin -z` per scan; failure/absence logs a warning and the remaining filters still apply (scan never errors).
5. Session-scope filter feeds `changed`/`untracked` too, so report counts and REFACTOR-comment/work-item creation can never reference an excluded path.

## Verification so far
- `pytest tests/test_refactor` → 227 passed (29 new).
- `ruff check skill/refactor tests/test_refactor` → clean.
- Real-worktree full-project scan via `detect_session_files(full_project=True)` → 504 files, 0 external leaks, 261 `skill/`, 4 `command/`, 210 `tests/` files retained.
- `refactor.py SA-0MVPDVXT90067E3M --dry-run --json` → 8 session files, 0 smells, 0 work items.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Design notes (Map) - Session ID: 01a18a0e-3806-708e-b862-ad7c4bffde55

**Baseline finding.** The per-checkout finish lock already landed on `dev` in WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84 (commit 65619fc10), inlined in `implement.py`. This item therefore closed the remaining gaps rather than re-implementing it:

1. **Shared helper** — extracted the flock mechanics into `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` (`RepoLock`, sibling to `process_semaphore.py` / `work_item_lock.py`) as the AC and Key Files asked. `implement.py` keeps `acquire_main_checkout_lock` / `_release_main_checkout_lock` / `_main_checkout_lock_path` as thin wrappers, so existing pins and callers are unchanged.
2. **Bounded wait + timeout message** — `RepoLock.acquire(holder_id, timeout)`: `0` (default) = fail fast; `>0` = wait to a deadline then refuse with an actionable message naming the lock path, the holder, the expired deadline and the recovery step. `timeout=None` is rejected (no indefinite hang). `finish` opts in via `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 0 = fail fast, which AC3 explicitly permits); the report records `timeout_seconds`.
3. **Adjacent dev-mutating window covered** — `phase_start`'s pre-worktree parent-branch refresh fast-forwards the same shared local ref a finish moves, so it now takes the same lock (`_sync_parent_branch_locked`), **fail-open**: bounded by `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 30s), then skips with `reason: lock_held` and a warning. A start is never blocked or failed by a concurrent finish.
4. **Deliberate exclusions** — `_restore_repo_state` stays unlocked (abort path; the process may already hold the lock and the kernel releases it on death). Documented in its docstring.

Assumption: holder metadata (pid/started_at/host) stays in the lock file for refusal messages only and never decides ownership — the AC's "no PID or timestamp bookkeeping" is read as "nothing but the flock decides ownership", which the F1 contract (test_leftover_lock_file_does_not_block_a_later_finish) also pins.

Docs: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` lock section updated (helper location, bounded wait, start window, recovery).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation notes (design decision + AC coverage).

**Design choice (from the parent plan's open implementation constraint):** the pre-push local-`dev` fast-forward is *kept* (so the dev-push context-budget gate measures the main checkout with the new files present) but is now **loud and reversible**, and it is no longer the authority on publication. Post-push, `finish` asserts its own commit (including a rebased replacement hash) is an ancestor of `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and fails closed naming the hash. Both AC1 and AC2 are therefore satisfied without losing the pre-push gate property.

**AC1 — verified/reversible local-dev sync:**
- `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push()` replaces the silent `except Exception`: fetch + resolve the remote tip, refuse loudly (naming refs/hashes) when local `dev` carries commits origin lacks, has diverged, checkout/fetch fails, or the finish commit is not based on the remote tip; never rewrites history (`--ff-only` only); records `pre_advance_tip`/`own_churn`.
- `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push()` runs on every push-failure path (generic failure, `PushTimeoutError`, `PushNonFastForwardError`) and returns local `dev` to `refs/remotes/origin/dev` via `reset --merge` (never `--hard`, uncommitted work preserved) or an atomic compare-and-swap `update-ref`; it never clobbers a branch another actor moved.
- `_sync_parent_branch()` (post-push) already only fast-forwards to the remote-tracking ref; it now reports the `target` so the property is observable.

**AC2 — ancestry assertion:** `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` + `AncestryAssertionError`; the short hash reported by `git_get_commit_hash` is resolved to its full object name before `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. On refusal the worktree and feature branch are retained, the item stays `open` (never `in_review`), and the refusal is commented on the item.

**Tests:** new `tests/test_implement_finish_local_dev_verified_sync.py` (hermetic bare-remote + clone sandbox) covers the advance, every refusal path, restore (incl. uncommitted-work and concurrent-actor safety), post-push sync target and the assertion pass/fail/unresolvable paths; extended `test_implement_finish_concurrent_orphan.py`, `test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` and `test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` (rebased replacement hash).

**Assumption:** all `finish` sessions for a repository share one filesystem (documented in the parent item), so the F2 flock plus this ancestry assertion are jointly sufficient.

## Slice complete — commit `5f902db9c` (pushed to `dev`)

**Deliverable:** `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py` (new, 707 lines) — subprocess-level two-holder concurrency regression. No production code ships in this slice (test-first slice; `phase_start` is wired by SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3).

### How the race is made deterministic (no sleep-based windows)
Two plain `start` processes race nondeterministically, so the winner is held *inside* its critical section: a test-only `git` shim on the winner's `PATH` signals readiness on a FIFO and blocks on an exclusive `flock` immediately before `git worktree add`. The test holds that flock, starts the winner, waits for readiness with `select`, starts the loser, joins it, snapshots, then releases the winner. While the loser runs, the winner is provably alive and holding the child lock. Every contender is a real `python3 skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start <id> --json` process against a throwaway git repo + real `wl` store (`QZ-…` prefix so the shared resolver never reaches this repo's store).

### AC coverage
- **AC1 / parent-AC1 (mutual exclusion)** — `test_only_one_of_two_concurrent_starts_acquires_the_child_lock`: lock file records the winner's pid; an independent cross-process `WorkItemLock.acquire()` is refused while the winner runs; the loser reports `success: false`, `action: "skipped-held"`, `held_by: {agent, pid, session_id, started_at}` naming the winner's pid, and exits non-zero.
- **AC2 (loser is side-effect free)** — `test_loser_performs_no_writes_worktree_or_status_mutation`: SHA-256 snapshot of every file in the worklog store + `git status` + `git worktree list` is byte-identical before and after the loser runs; no state file, no worktree, no claim/comment.
- **AC3 (no divergence from the winner's writes)** — `test_winner_files_are_not_diverged_by_the_loser`: exactly one worktree, its `.implement_state.json` is the winner's (id/path/repo_root/parent_branch), the worktree holds only that one write (`?? .implement_state.json`), the item has exactly one "Implementation started" comment (no resumed/aborted comments) and is `in-progress`.
- **AC4 (real subprocess boundary)** — every assertion reads real subprocesses; nothing mocks `phase_start` or the lock.
- **AC5 (SIGTERM release + stale-dead-pid reclamation with warning)** — covered by the shared unit slice `skill/shared/tests/test_work_item_lock.py` (`test_sigterm_killed_holder_releases_kernel_lock`, `test_stale_dead_pid_lock_is_reclaimed_with_warning`); deliberately not duplicated (anti-pattern: duplicates of existing core coverage). Subprocess-level counterpart added here: `test_lock_is_released_when_the_winner_exits` (completed start → later start succeeds with `resumed: true` and the new pid recorded).
- **parent-AC5 (regression test)** — this module.

That file is the executable contract for the `phase_start` side of this slice. The test snapshots every file under the worklog store (sha256) plus `git status` and `git worktree list`, and requires a byte-identical snapshot across the loser's run.
4. The winner holds the lock for the whole of `phase_start` and releases it on process exit: a later `start` succeeds (`resumed: true`) with the lock file recording the new pid, i.e. the recorded dead pid is reclaimed without blocking.
5. The contender's env has `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` stripped, so the loser must be refused on token mismatch — token propagation must not accidentally make unrelated processes self-owned.

## F2 implementation notes

**Reproduction (hermetic, finish-gate entry point)** — extends F1's harness in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` with a disk-reading parity fixture: a generated wiki registry (`_build/registry.json`, gitignored generated metadata) compared against the on-disk document set by a parity test that never invokes git. The seed commit is green; the change set adds `wiki/synthesis.md` without rebuilding the registry, so the gate's own tree is red.

**Named mechanism:** a green verdict served for a *different tree*. `compute_git_state` fingerprints HEAD plus every path `git status` reports, so gitignored generated metadata is invisible to the cache key and the key carries no checkout identity. The fixture records a **real** green suite run against the rebuilt-metadata tree (asserting the loose fingerprint is unchanged by the rebuild), restores the lagging registry, and the gate serves that entry: `{"scope": "full", "success": true}` for a tree whose suite is red. Untracked-file invisibility (F1) cannot explain it — the suite reads disk only.

**Tests added**
- `test_parity_verdict_reflects_the_gate_tree_when_the_suite_genuinely_runs` — no cache entry: red verdict naming the parity test (the verdict follows the tree that ran).
- `test_baseline_capture_parity_false_pass_from_a_foreign_cache_entry` — captured false green; asserts the entry was *served* (`completed_at` unchanged) and that the same tree is red when its suite runs.
- `test_parity_foreign_cache_entry_misses_once_f7_lands` — strict `xfail` until F7 (SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB): entry must miss, suite re-runs red, parity test named; asserts the entry's fingerprint differs from `git write-tree` over a temp-index staged would-be-commit tree. F7 removes the marker and inverts the baseline capture (documented in both docstrings and the xfail reason).
- `tests/test_test_cache.py::test_generated_metadata_is_invisible_to_the_git_state_fingerprint` — cache-layer pin for the same blindness (one execution, then a served green verdict for a different on-disk metadata state).

**Root cause recorded on the parent** — comment SA-C0MVU88BSA00979ME on SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2: named mechanism (stale/foreign cache entry from a different tree), evidence trail (2751 vs 2781 collected; 08:53 `8e9c3ea7` vs 10:56 `f73d063e`; per-worktree entry unrecoverable → documented causal argument, plan Q2=a), and the consequence that F7 (tree-fingerprint binding) is the necessary closure for the parity case — the F6 temp index alone cannot close a disk-reading suite.

**Assumption recorded:** the historical gate's per-worktree cache entry is unrecoverable, so the fixture models the collision mechanism (shared fingerprint across tree states) rather than replaying the exact historical entry — the operator-approved evidence standard (plan Q2=a). No production code changed; F6/F7 own the fix.

# Plan Complete — feature decomposition

Decomposed SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB into 6 child features (test-first order), with
a 100% AC-coverage review (`proceed`). Effort/risk pre-check returned
`decision: plan` (Small / Medium risk); the plan-approval gate returned
`request_approval: false` (approval is reserved for Extra Large **and** High+
risk), so the six automated review stages ran without an approval pause.

## Features (execution order)

| # | Child | Type | Parent ACs | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F0 | Baseline regression tests for full-suite resolution (SA-0MVQQ9HXV000V6Z4) | task | AC2 (zero-candidate clause), AC7 baseline | — |
| F1 | Detect and emit hidden skill-test pytest command (SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS) | task | AC1, AC2 | F0 |
| F2 | Pinned suiteCommands precedence and no-double-execution (SA-0MVQQ9NV4005UKYZ) | task | AC3, AC4 | F1 |
| F3 | Groups, types and consumer parity for hidden skill tests (SA-0MVQQ9QJI002K7DY) | task | AC5, AC6, AC7 | F1, F2 |
| F4 | Document hidden skill-test resolution rule (SA-0MVQQ9T7Z0009F8C) | docs | AC8 | F1, F2, F3 |
| F5 | Verify full suite green and hand off to llm consumer (SA-0MVQQ9VR7000OB7H) | task | AC9, AC10 | F3, F4 |

**Why F0 first (test-first).** The parent's two hardest guarantees — "zero
candidates → byte-identical resolution" (D2) and "changed-scope untouched"
(D5) — are *preservation* properties. Pinning them as green tests before any
resolver change is the only way to prove later slices did not regress them,
and it satisfies test-first ordering without a red tree (a red intermediate
tree would violate the dev-push gate). Each implementation child (F1–F3) then
applies TDD internally: tests express the AC, then the resolver change lands
in the same commit.

## Design decisions recorded (not silent assumptions)

- **D-A1 — Notice surface (elaborating D3/AC3).** `full_suite_commands()`
  keeps its `list[str]` signature (D4 — no consumer sees a signature change).
  The machine-readable notice is exposed by a new pure accessor
  (`hidden_skill_test_notice()` / `full_suite_notices()`) carrying a stable
  code (`hidden_skill_tests_uncovered`) plus the uncovered directory list, and
  `run_tests.py` surfaces it non-fatally (JSON `resolution_notices` + one
  stderr warning line, exit status unchanged). Recorded in F2 AC3/AC4b.
- **D-A2 — No-double-execution skip rule (elaborating D3/AC4).** A candidate
  counts as "already collected" only when a `testpaths`/`addopts` token
  resolves to `.pi` or a **strict descendant** of `.pi` and the candidate is
  a descendant-or-equal of it. Tokens at or above the repo root (`.`, `tests`,
  `skill`) do **not** count: pytest's default `norecursedirs` (`.*`) still
  prunes `.pi` from those roots, so treating them as coverage would silently
  re-silence exactly the tests this item exists to surface. Custom
  `norecursedirs`/`--ignore` overrides are explicitly out of scope. Recorded
  in F2.
- **D-A3 — End-to-end proof lives on the consumer.** This repo has no
  `.pi/skills`, so its own command set must stay byte-identical (asserted by
  F0 AC2). The behavioural proof of the new rule is unit-level here (F1–F3)
  plus end-to-end on LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X (parent AC10, owned there). F5
  records the downstream verification checklist as a comment on the consumer
  item rather than editing the llm repo.

## Housekeeping

The AC-coverage helper auto-created two stub children from conservative fuzzy
matches (score 0.375 / no match) because the child AC wording diverged from
the parent's. Both duplicated existing scope and were closed as duplicates:

- SA-0MVQQBX9W004IULO → duplicate of F2 (parent AC4).
- SA-0MVQQBYFF009KUBV → duplicate of F4 (parent AC8).

The F2/F4 AC first lines were then aligned with the parent AC text so a re-run
of the coverage review is idempotent (`proceed`, 100%, no new children).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required: the intake brief already answers the
plan-level questions, and the producer's decision round recorded in the brief's
comment (SA-C0MVQJSW7Y0059WHF) fixed the two contested points.

- **Q: Should the extra command be one per directory or one command listing
  all candidates?** Answer (producer, via the brief's D2 + comment
  SA-C0MVQJSW7Y0059WHF): one command listing all, to keep a single cache
  entry, a single timeout budget and unchanged semaphore accounting
  (`run_tests.py` acquires one host-wide slot per suite execution). Final:
  one command (D2, F1).
- **Q: Does the new rule override a project's pinned `suiteCommands`?**
  Answer (producer, SA-C0MVQJSW7Y0059WHF): no — projects may supply local
  test-skill configuration, so a pinned list is returned verbatim and the
  uncovered hidden skill test dirs are surfaced as a machine-readable notice
  instead. Final: pin wins, notice informs (D3, AC3, F2).
- **Q: Coverage breadth — the single skill that ships tests today, or all
  `.pi/skills/*` test directories?** Answer (producer,
  SA-C0MVQJSW7Y0059WHF): all of them (glob form). Final: all candidates
  (D1, F1).
- **Q: Where exactly does the machine-readable notice surface?** —
  **DOCUMENTED ASSUMPTION (D-A1)**, producer confirmation welcome but not
  blocking: a pure accessor plus non-fatal runner reporting (`--json`
  `resolution_notices`, stderr warning), signature of
  `full_suite_commands()` unchanged. Evidence for the choice: D4's "no
  consumer changes" constraint plus the existing `NOTICE_*` code convention
  in `run_tests.py`.
- **Q: Do `testpaths`/`addopts` tokens at or above the repo root count as
  "already collected"?** — **DOCUMENTED ASSUMPTION (D-A2)**: no, because the
  default `norecursedirs` (`.*`) means such roots never reach `.pi/`. Only
  tokens at/under `.pi` suppress a candidate. Evidence: the brief's root-cause
  row (`pytest_ignore_collect` skips explicit initial paths only) and the
  measured 5 264 vs 529 totals on LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X.
- **Q: Should changed-scope selection also pick hidden skill tests?** Answer
  (brief D5): out of scope — heuristic fast-feedback only; the full gate is
  the enforcement point. Final: unchanged (F3 AC7).

- 2026-10-27T13:35Z — Planned SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB: created 6 child features

  `plan_complete` (coverage review: `proceed`, 100%).

data.comment:
Resolved — host environment remediation (no code change required).

## Root cause
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and runs the real worker (`pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `import numpy as np` at line 117). On this host `/usr/bin/python3` is a bare Python 3.12 with neither `numpy` nor `faster-whisper` available, so every transcription subtest surfaced `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` (and the two 20 s waits timed out). `pytest`, `node --test tests/node/**` and `node --test tests/cli/**` all passed; only `tests/unit` failed.

## Provenance (pre-existing, not a regression)
- Cache history for `node --test 'tests/unit/**/*.mjs'`: green through 2026-09-26, **red from 2026-10-15** (also red 2026-10-21), i.e. the gap predates this session's change.
- No repository change caused it: numpy was introduced in `e2218e77` long before the failures started; the failure is purely the missing interpreter dependency.

## Remediation
- `python3 -m pip install --user --break-system-packages numpy` → `numpy 2.5.4` installed to `~/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages` (the voice-input README documents `python3 -m pip install faster-whisper` as the setup path; numpy is its runtime dependency). Per-user install only — no system package change, no probe of the LLM proxy or other services.

## Verification
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full --force` at SorraAgents HEAD `d639d615`: **rc 0**, node suite `tests 814 / suites 184 / pass 814 / fail 0`, pytest green. Post-push read-only `--summary --suite all` reports a cached green full-suite entry (`missing: []`).

## Follow-up worth considering (not done here — scope)
The unit node suite silently depended on a host-wide `numpy` that is not declared anywhere in the repo (no `requirements.txt`). A future chore could add a `requires-python`-dependency manifest or a `skip`-when-missing guard so the suite is self-describing on a bare interpreter.

Discovered while implementing LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 (audit child-screen green-run evidence); that item was blocked by this failure at the dev-push gate.

Implementation complete — commit a624d18ed pushed to dev.

**What changed**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - New helpers: `_work_item_prefix`, `_is_same_project`, `_blocker_payload`, `_format_blockers`, `_outbound_gate` (resolves the invoked item's own `wl_dep_blockers` and splits unmet same-project blockers from cross-project coordination notes; terminal/soft-deleted blockers never gate, matching `_is_terminal_child`).
  - `phase_parent` Step 3.5 (new): the parent's own outbound blockers and its own `status: blocked` are resolved **before** any child classification. Verdict is a dedicated soft `blocked` report — `blocked: true`, `parent_blocked_by` (ids+statuses+titles), `parent_blocked_reason` (`outbound-dependency` / `status-blocked` / both joined by `+`), no `next_child`, no `parent_advanced`, `success` stays true; every child is reported as `blocked-parent` and no worktree is created (AC1/AC2).
  - `phase_parent` child classification: a child blocked by a **same-project** item outside the epic is now reported `blocked` (with a `blocked_by` payload, listed in `blocked_children` when another child is started) instead of being started into a refusal; cross-project child edges stay `external_blockers` coordination notes (unchanged).
  - `phase_start` / `_phase_start_locked` Step 3.0 (new): the leaf gate refuses with `blocked: true` + `blocked_by` **before the claim**, so a blocked leaf is never left `in_progress` with no worktree (Assumption A3). It runs *under* the per-child lock because a losing lock contender must leave the worklog store byte-identical (`test_drive_child_lock.py::test_loser_performs_no_writes_worktree_or_status_mutation` pins this).
  - `phase_drive`: a parent report with `blocked` stops the loop, forwards `parent_blocked_by`/`parent_blocked_reason`, spawns **no** session, keeps `success: true`, and never sets `failed_child` — a soft producer-mandated wait, distinct from a hard failure.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1: documents the invoked item's own outbound gate (parent + leaf), the blocked report vocabulary, and clarifies the external-blocker wording — the SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T 'coordination note' assumption covers **cross-project** edges only, not same-project edges recorded on the invoked parent itself (AC5).
- Tests (TDD — written first, red then green): `tests/test_implement_parent_outbound_gate.py` (11 cases: parent blocked by unmet edge, parent queried before classification, all children `blocked-parent`, blocked+edge reason, A1 status-only block, only unmet blockers reported, no-edge/terminal/soft-deleted unchanged, cross-project note, in-chain ordering unchanged, same-project out-of-chain child blocked, drive forwarding) and `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_outbound_gate.py` (6 cases: refuse with blocker list, no worktree, terminal proceeds, soft-deleted proceeds, cross-project note, no edges proceeds).

Cross-project edges on the invoked item are reported in `coordination_blockers` and never gate, preserving the documented SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T assumption while still closing the same-project parent-level gap this item targets.

**A1 — implemented per plan default, producer confirmation still open (non-blocking).** A parent with `status: blocked` and **no** outbound edges also waits. Note discovered while implementing: `wl dep add` auto-sets the dependent item's status to `blocked` and nothing clears it when the dependency completes (4 items in this store are in that stale state). The gate therefore never silently overrides the status, but the message names the remedy (`wl update <id> --status open`) so a stale auto-block is one command away from unblocking.

Additional production evidence for this defect, plus two adjacent scope notes.

**Evidence (2026-10-29, `llm` project, audit of LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG).** A downtime-dispatched
`audit_runner.py issue LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG` run emitted **nine** in-main-slot screens (6 Phase-1 child AC
screens + 3 Phase-2 child deep analyses for the non-XS/low-risk children), persisted six child audits with
pending `partial` ACs and no `auditedAt`, wrote
`.worklog/audit-checkpoints/LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG.pending-screens.json`, and finished `Ready to close: No` with the
`Child screens pending: 6 (main-slot)` gate. The invoking session could not service the screens, so the resume
cycle this item describes was never even attempted; log:
`~/.audit_debug/llm/audit-LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG-20261029T004409.log`.

**This is not a one-off.** Seven items currently carry unserviced signals, dating back two weeks:

```
LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI  2 children   2026-10-15
LP-0MVB8F5ZU0079DE9  1            2026-10-20
LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4  1            2026-10-18
LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY  3            2026-10-23
LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0  2            2026-10-29  (the case this item was written from)
LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X  3            2026-10-29
LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG  6            2026-10-29
```

**Adjacent scope note 1 — dispatched vs interactive audits.** In-main-slot mode assumes an interactive invoking
session that can run each screen inline and `/compact` between children. A herdr-downtime-dispatched audit is
non-interactive by nature, so every dispatched parent audit lands in the unserviced state by construction. Suggest
the dispatcher (or `cmd_issue` when it detects a dispatched/non-interactive context) pass
`--no-child-in-main-slot`, so a dispatched audit performs child screens in isolated `pi` subprocesses with the
runner's own parsing/retry instead of emitting prompts nobody will run. This is a policy choice, adjacent to — but
distinct from — the D1/D2 resume defects here.

**Adjacent scope note 2 — stale-signal sweep.** Once D1/D2 land, the seven signals above need a one-off sweep
(forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` runs) so the existing backlog does not keep constraining readiness decisions; they
are also the natural fixtures for verifying the fix.

Fixed in production by: parent LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG was amended to the `local-preferred` deferrable/too-large split

## Plan: changelog

Planned 2026-10-30 (plan session `herdr-1793320606-739649-10404`). Decision: full plan (effort/risk pre-check returned `plan`; approval gate `request_approval: false`, so no approval pause).

- Decomposed into 5 vertical slices, **test-first**: contract fixtures/tests → runner facts → finish-gate classification → queue-wait proof → docs.
- Created children (in dependency order):
  1. **SA-0MVU8XQTU006DP37** Test: gate classification fixtures and contract
  2. **SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D** Runner: duration, timeout, kill and unparsed facts
  3. **SA-0MVU8XRTE008VDO2** Finish gate: timeout, kill and unparsed reasons
  4. **SA-0MVU8XSGI003DBWR** Prove queue wait is outside the timeout budget
  5. **SA-0MVU8XT1M002MSJX** Docs: classification fields in skill references
- Dependency edges wired: 2→1, 3→2, 4→3, 5→4 (`wl dep list` on each child).
- AC coverage review (`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py run-coverage-review`): **proceed**, 100% of parent ACs covered, no gaps auto-closed, no conflicts.
- `**Key Files:**` sections validated (`validate_key_files_format`) and every listed path confirmed to exist.
- Effort/risk estimate applied via the effort-and-risk skill (WBS across the 5 children).

## Design decisions carried into the children

- **One wait measurement.** The slot-queue wait is measured once, by the existing `paced_runner(on_wait=...)` callback (SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 / SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO), and reported as its own `slot_wait_seconds`. No second timer is added.
- **`elapsed_seconds` excludes the wait** by construction: it is measured around the subprocess execution only, so the per-command timeout budget and the reported elapsed time share one boundary (parent AC4).
- **Stable codes, never text matching.** Runner emits `suite_timeout` (existing), plus new `killed` (signal-terminated, `returncode < 0`) and `unparsed_failure` (non-zero exit with no parsable failures); `slot_busy` unchanged. Finish gate maps codes to distinct reasons `timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed`, keeping `slot_contention`/`infrastructure`/`test_failure`.
- **`unknown` survives only as a documented last resort**, with a non-empty detail, and is unreachable for timed-out, killed or non-zero runs (parent AC1/AC2).
- **Cached failures are classified too:** a non-zero result served from cache has no elapsed time, so it is reported as `unparsed_failure`/`killed` with `elapsed_seconds: null` (never `0`). This is an in-scope extension of parent AC2 discovered during planning — the cache stores exit code and output already.
- Scope guard: no `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` change, no semaphore bypass; slot fairness/starvation remains with SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No blocking questions were asked: the parent description carries measured evidence, requirements, constraints and predicted key files, so the decomposition was derivable without producer input. Assumptions and non-blocking open questions are recorded below instead.

### Assumptions (proposed, not confirmed by a producer)

1. The `on_wait` pacer measurement is the single source of the slot-wait duration (no second timer) — per the related item SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO, which was verified as `open`/`idea` (no shipped telemetry store yet), so its future aggregation can reuse `slot_wait_seconds` rather than re-measuring.
2. `timeoutPerCommand` is applied to the subprocess only; where an outer command timeout bounds the whole invocation (agent shell / harness), the wait is reported separately rather than subtracted — the parent's AC4 "or" branch.
3. Signal-terminated children are detected from a negative `subprocess` return code (OOM killer and worker crashes both surface this way); no cgroup/OOM log inspection is attempted.
4. Failure parsing stays as-is (pytest/node parsers); the new codes apply only when `failures` is empty, so structured failures always win.
5. Changes land in the SorraAgents framework source (`skill/test`, `skill/implement`, `docs/dev`), then reach consumers via `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

### OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking — proposed default recorded)

- Q: Do you prefer `killed` or `signal_killed` as the stable notice code for a signal-terminated run, and `killed` or `signal_killed` as the gate reason? **Proposed default:** `killed` for both (shortest, matches "is killed" in the parent AC). Changing it later is a rename of one constant plus docs — it does not affect the plan or the dependency order. Directed to the producer because the code is operator-visible in gate output.
- Q: Should the dev-push pre-push gate also surface these classification fields (it consumes the same `run_tests.py` output), or is that follow-up work? **Proposed default:** out of scope here — the runner emits the fields, so the pre-push gate can adopt them without further runner work. Directed to the producer because it could add a sixth child (a small pre-push reporting slice) if wanted.

## Tracer-bullet conventions used (read before auditing)

**Deliverable is tests only** (per the parent plan's slice 1: "tests + no production change"). Production changes belong to SA-0MVTU2268007BBYO (`--json` on the subparser) and SA-0MVTU22MB0057T2L (post-remediation content-freshness resolution).

Because two behaviour specs legitimately cannot pass before their implementation sibling lands, they use the repo's established tracer-bullet conventions:

- **pytest:** `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` (same convention as `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` and `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`). A strict unexpected pass is itself a failure, so the marker cannot be silently retained.
  - `test_check_freshness_subcommand_accepts_json_flag`
  - `test_check_freshness_json_flag_leaves_the_payload_unchanged`
  - **Owner removes the marker:** SA-0MVTU2268007BBYO (its AC requires this pin test to pass).
- **node:test:** `{ skip: '<reason naming the sibling>' }` — `node:test` has no strict-xfail equivalent, and a `todo` marker would be parsed as a `not ok` line by `run_tests.py::parse_node_failures` (failing the gate even on exit 0), so `skip` is the only safe convention here. The bodies are complete, not placeholders.
  - `attemptAuditRemediation` post-remediation (content-fresh → passing; content-changed → `time-stale but content changed` + `--force`)
  - the no-`Ready to close`-block invariant matrix (6 audit fixtures × 3 probe replies)
  - the ContextHub regression, in both gates
  - **Owner removes the markers:** SA-0MVTU22MB0057T2L (its AC says the invariant test must stay green).

## Red-for-the-right-reason evidence (verified, no suite run)

A throwaway diagnostic script drove the real modules with the same injected boundaries as the specs:

| Spec | Current production result | Fails at |
|---|---|---|
| post-remediation, probe content-fresh | `status: 'blocking'`, reason `Ready to close` | expected `passing` |
| post-remediation, probe content-changed | `status: 'blocking'`, reason `Ready to close` (not the real condition) | `/time-stale but content changed/` |
| invariant, passing+v2 audit / probe not fresh | blocking entry with reason `Ready to close` | negative invariant |
| invariant, passing+legacy or passing+no-fingerprint (any probe) | blocking entry with reason `Ready to close` | negative invariant |
| ContextHub regression (both gates) | `hasBlockingItems: true`, item not remediated | `hasBlockingItems === false` |

The green specs already pass against today's code: the exact probe argv pin, the upgrade-by-content-freshness test in **both** gates through the real `queryContentFreshness()` parse (stubbed `runCommand` only), and the fail-open fallback (an inconclusive probe still re-audits and blocks).

- `check-final-validation.js` imports `queryContentFreshness` without re-exporting it, so the Step-3.7 specs import the real probe from its source of truth (`check-audit-gate.js`) and stub only `runCommand`/`resolveAuditRunnerFn` — the gates' behaviour is unchanged and no production export was added.

- **SA-0MVU5XZKG005Y61S** (discovered-from this item): `run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` does not recognise the repo's dominant `test-*.mjs` node naming, so a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file selects **no** node command in the changed-scope gate (43 of 44 files affected). data.author: plan
data.comment:
question: **Q1 — what is the scope of the live-evidence AC (AC6)?**

The origin epic `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) now has **three** `blocked` children — `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` — and one **`open`** child, `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, held only by `assignee: Map` + the `do-not-delegate` tag (its `blocked` status could not be stored: `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82`). `phase_parent` honours neither assignee holds nor `do-not-delegate` (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`), so the post-fix run will still start that `open` child — while AC6 as written says the run "starts nothing".

Options:
- **(A)** scope AC6 to "none of the three `blocked` children is started; all three reported `skip-blocked` with their `SA-…` ids", and report the open held child truthfully with a cross-reference to `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`.
- **(B)** widen this item to also gate on `do-not-delegate`/assignee holds (overlaps `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, already planned and `blocked`).
- **(C)** prove the behaviour on a synthetic fixture epic in this repo and record the MS run as pending until `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876` lands.

**Recommended:** A — it proves exactly the bug this item owns (a `blocked` child is never started) without duplicating the do-not-delegate item, and keeps the live evidence honest about what the run actually did.

Why it matters: it decides whether C6 (`SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`) can be executed at all, and whether the MS epic stays held after this fix lands. Recorded in the parent description Appendix as **OPEN QUESTION**.

data.author: plan
data.comment:
question: **Q2 — when a block is found stale, should the child's lifecycle status be refreshed, or only the start allowed?**

AC2 says the child "is startable again (and the stale block is named in the report/log)"; the Goal paragraph adds "(or its status refreshed)".

Options:
- **(A)** start the child and report/log the stale block, leaving the `blocked` status to the lifecycle owner (a comment on the child records the stale finding).
- **(B)** also flip the child to `open` via `StatusLifecycle` with an audit comment before starting.
- **(C)** flip to `open` and clear/annotate the prose `Blocked by` line.

**Recommended:** A — it never silently erases a producer-set hold, keeps `phase_parent` a reader of lifecycle state rather than a writer of it, and `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82` shows blocked-status writes are unreliable in `wl`.

Why it matters: it determines whether C2 (`SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW`) mutates child status, and therefore whether it needs the `StatusLifecycle` audit-comment path. Recorded in the parent description Appendix as **OPEN QUESTION**.

data.author: plan
data.comment:
question: **Q3 — should a cross-project prose blocker be resolved through the sibling worklog scan (so a landed external blocker makes the block stale)?**

`implement.py` already routes `wl` calls through `shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`, whose prefix-to-sibling scan maps an id prefix to its owning project's worklog. Verified 2026-10-30 from `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`: prefix `SA` resolves to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog`, `MS` to the tce worklog — so resolution is available with no network call.

Options:
- **(A)** resolve cross-project ids through that scan: terminal → stale (child startable), non-terminal → holds, and only a genuinely unresolvable id holds as unvalidated.
- **(B)** do not resolve cross-repo — every cross-project id holds, and the child's owner must refresh the child when the external item lands.
- **(C)** resolve opportunistically (try the scan, fall back to holds) but never cache the result.

**Recommended:** A — it is what makes the origin epic self-unblocking when the three `SA-…` items land, which is the inverse failure the Goal names ("a stale block must not strand a child forever"); B leaves three MS children stranded forever and contradicts that Goal.

Why it matters: it changes C3's (`SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB`) acceptance criteria and tests materially. Recorded in the parent description Appendix as **OPEN QUESTION**.

data.comment:
Implementation complete and pushed to dev.

**Commit:** c34fd7d91 — SA-0MVTV8WQ00014DSK: isolate F7 harness from host ingress cap and clean up temp worklog

**Root cause (reproduced, not load-dependent).** The F7 harness launches 8 concurrent `audit_runner.py issue` processes, but the harness never set the host-wide *ingress* cap (`AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS`, default 6). Two audits therefore queued at ingress; under host load the bounded ingress wait (`AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, default 90 s) expired and those audits exited 1, so `batch.ok` was false and validate_fanout exited 1 with empty stderr — exactly the reported signature. Deterministic repro before the fix: `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS=6 AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=0 python3 skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` → exit 1, two results carrying 'host-wide audit concurrency limit reached'.

**Fix.**
1. `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` sets `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS` to the batch size: the semaphore dir is already per-batch, so the ingress cap protects nothing real here and the pi ceiling (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`) is the only binding constraint being measured (the F7 capacity runs lifted the cap to 32 by hand for the same reason).
2. The harness now removes its throwaway `f7-validate-*` worklog tree (740 such trees / ~228 MB plus inodes had accumulated in /tmp, feeding the EDQUOT pressure behind SA-0MVTSV5SO008625I).
3. `results[].stderr_tail` widened to 500 chars and the tests name failing audit indices + stderr tails, so a future batch failure is diagnosable from the assertion message.
4. Tests write reports to `tmp_path` instead of fixed `/tmp/f7-report-*.json` (concurrent suite runs on a shared host overwrote each other's reports) and a new regression test pins the ingress-cap isolation + temp-tree cleanup with a fail-fast ingress environment.

**Verification.** Changed scope: 7/7 pass. Full suite at the pushed commit c34fd7d91 (`run_tests.py --scope full`, executed fresh): pytest 5163 passed / 15 skipped, node suites 818/818 — 0 failures.
